title: Activity Log
text: The Activity Log tab contains the history of changes related to the selected guest. Activity Log The log displays the date and time of the change, the employee or system that performed the action, the type of change, and related details. For example, the log records tags being added or removed, changes to notes, preferences, and RFM Status. Data Filtering Activity Log Filter To filter the Activity Log, click Filters. After selecting the required values, click Apply. Applied filters are displayed above the table. To remove an individual filter, click × next to its name. To reset all filters, click Clear Filters. Note. Selected filters are saved after the page is refreshed and when switching between guest profiles. The filters are reset after you log out.

title: Call History
text: Call History is a table view of the reservation module that shows phone calls received through the telephony integration. One row is one call. The call history helps you: handle incoming calls; keep track of missed calls; assess how many calls end with a reservation. To open the call history, click the phone icon in the left menu of the reservation module. Call History Call Info Click a call row to open the Call Info sidebar. It shows the call type, status, time and duration, the guest and the phone number. If a reservation was created from the call, it is shown in the Linked Reservation block. Click the reservation to open it in view mode. The Changelogs button in the reservation opens the list of all changes to this reservation. Call Info Linked Reservation Changelogs To open the Guest Info sidebar, click the block with the guest's name in the open reservation. It has two tabs: Profile — the guest's RFM segment, autotags and manual tags, loyalty number, loyalty bonuses, discount, sex and last visit date. You can also add a manual tag to the guest here; Statistics — the guest's visit statistics. Guest Info Statistics To open the statistics, click the button in the lower-right corner of the table. The statistics have two tabs: Calls and Conversion. On both tabs, the data is split into incoming and outgoing calls. Calls Conversion The Calls tab shows: Total — the total number of calls; Incoming — calls that are coming in right now; Accepted Completed Missed Avg Duration — the average call duration. The Conversion tab shows: Reservation Conversion — the share of calls that resulted in a reservation; Reservations Created — the number of reservations created from calls. Table Settings To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ Select the columns to display ✔ Change the column order — drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name ✔ Pin the required columns — click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table ✔ Restore the default settings using Reset to Default Table Settings By default, the table displays the following columns: Call Type — incoming or outgoing Call Status Missed Status — for missed calls: Didn't call back, Didn't get through, Called back or Guest called back Call Time — the date and time the call started Duration Guest — the guest's name and RFM segment Phone Reservation Status — the status of the reservation created from the call Filters Click Filters, select a parameter on the left, check the required values and click Apply. Filters You can filter calls by: Call Status — Incoming, Accepted, Completed, Missed Call Type — Incoming, Outgoing Missed Status — Didn't call back, Didn't get through, Called back, Guest called back Reservation Status — Not Confirmed, Confirmed, Started, Ended, Cancelled, Waitlist

title: Create and Configure
text: To create a widget: Click Create in the upper right corner of the widget list. Fill in the fields in blocks 1–4 and select the form settings you need. Click Save. After saving, the Embed Code button appears in the upper right corner of the page — it opens the code for adding the widget to a website. See Adding to a Website for details. Widget Page 1\. Main Details Name — the widget name in the system. It is shown in the widget list and at the top of the widget page. Guests do not see it. Locations — locations where guests can submit a request. You can select several. Description — an optional note for staff, up to 250 characters. 2\. Design Title Background Accent Text Fields 3\. Field Configuration The following fields are always present in the form and are required: First Name Phone Location — not shown if the widget is linked to one location Reservation Date Time Duration Guests Consent to personal data processing Additional fields are turned on with the toggle on the left. A check in the Required column makes the field required. Last Name Date of Birth E-mail Telegram Comment Manual Tags — manual tag groups the guest can select, for example allergies. Groups with Available in Reservation Widget enabled in their settings are shown, under the group's public name if it is specified. See Create and Edit Manual Tags for details. 4\. Privacy Policy Link — the address of the privacy policy page on the venue website. Required field. Preview The Preview on the right shows changes immediately. The buttons above it switch between the phone and desktop views of the form. Field validation works in the preview when you click Submit a request. Preview Adding to a Website The Embed Code button appears in the upper right corner of the widget page after the widget is saved. It opens the How to embed code window with ready-made code and connection steps: The connection script is added to the beginning of the website's \<body>. A button that opens the widget in a modal window and/or an empty block where the form is shown directly on the page is created on the page. The widget parameters are passed to initBookingWidget(...). Both options can be used on the same website. It is enough to pass the contents of the window to the website developer. Embed Code This is how the widget looks on the venue website: Widget on the Website Editing, Duplicating and Deleting To edit a widget, open it from the list, make changes and click Save. The duplicate button next to Delete creates a full copy of the widget. Make the necessary changes to the copy and save it — this creates a new widget. Delete and Duplicate Buttons When deleting, the Delete Widget window appears. The widget is deleted permanently: the code on websites stops working, and requests through this widget no longer arrive. Deleting a Widget When saving changes, the Apply changes window appears. After editing, the code placed on websites may become outdated — update it on all websites where the widget is installed. This action cannot be undone.

title: Create and Edit
text: Creating an RFM Status To create a new RFM Status, click Edit, then Add RFM Status, fill in the fields, and click Add. Create RFM Status Status Name Color Description Recency (R) — determines how long ago the guest's last order should have been to match the status. If All Time is enabled, the day limit is removed and the guest's entire order history is included in the calculation. Frequency (F) — determines the minimum number of orders the guest must make during the selected period. Monetary (M) — determines the minimum amount the guest must spend during the selected period. After an RFM Status is created, the system automatically recalculates RFM and distributes guests according to the current rules. Editing an RFM Status After clicking Edit, the page switches to edit mode. Edit RFM Status On the editing page, you can make the following changes: Calculation Horizon. Specify the period in days used to calculate Frequency and Monetary. After the new settings are applied, the number of guests in the RFM Statuses will be recalculated. Changing Priority. Change the priority of RFM Statuses by dragging and dropping the rows. If a guest meets the conditions of several statuses at the same time, the status with the higher priority will be assigned. Adding an RFM Status. Editing an RFM Status. Click the row of the required RFM Status to change its parameters. After the changes are saved, the system automatically recalculates RFM and distributes guests according to the current rules. Deleting an RFM Status Click Edit. Right-click the required RFM Status. Select Delete RFM Status. Confirm the deletion. After an RFM Status is deleted, the system automatically recalculates RFM and distributes guests according to the current rules.

title: Create and Edit Manual Tags
text: Creating a Manual Tag Group To create a new Manual Tag group: Click Create. Fill in the group settings. Click Save. Create Manual Tag Group 1\. Name 2\. Locations 3\. Description 4\. Editable in Reservations — allows you to assign and remove tags from this group directly in the reservation system. 5\. Available in Waiter App — allows you to use tags from this group in the Waiter App. Assign to Guest — allows you to assign and remove tags from this group in the Waiter App. This setting becomes available only when Available in Waiter App is enabled. 7\. Available in Reservation Widget — allows you to display tags from this group in the Reservation Widget. When this setting is enabled, you can specify a public group name that will be displayed in the widget. 8\. Reservations Display — allows you to choose where the group tags will be displayed: in the guest profile, time slot, on the table, in the call widget, in the guest hint, and in the Reservation List. Creating a Tag To add a tag to a group: Click Add Tag. Fill in the tag settings. Click Add. Click Save for the changes to take effect. Create Tag 1\. Name 2\. Short Name 3\. Color 4\. Icon 5\. Hint Text Editing To change the settings of a group or its Manual Tags, open the required group, make the changes, and click Save. Deleting a Manual Tag Group To delete a Manual Tag group, open the actions menu in the group list or on the group page and select Delete. Confirm the deletion in the window that opens. When a group is deleted, all tags in the group are deleted and removed from all guests they were assigned to. Deleting a Manual Tag To delete a Manual Tag, open the tag group, remove the required tag from the list, and click Save. After deletion, the tag will be removed from all guests it was assigned to.

title: Create Auto Mailing
text: An Auto mailing starts automatically when a specified event occurs and works according to the configured conditions, schedule, and sending limits. To create an Auto mailing, go to Marketing → Mailings, select Auto, and click Create. Main Details Create Configure the main mailing settings: Type Mass — for informational messages not related to sales or service events Marketing — for promotional messages intended to encourage guests to make a purchase Service — for messages related to guest service or a specific service event Mailing Format One Channel - the message is sent through one selected channel Cascade - the message is sent through several channels one after another, see Cascade Extra Priority — enable this option if the mailing should be sent without taking the general limits into account Priority - the share of sending this mailing gets when several mailings are sent at the same time, see Mailings. Name Timezone - the timezone used by the delayed sending schedule. Segments Description Set Mailing Limits General limits do not apply to mailings with Extra Priority. If individual limits are configured for the mailing, they still apply. After completing the main details, click Next. Conditions Create Configure the conditions for triggering and sending the mailing: Trigger - the event that sends the mailing to a guest. The fields below the trigger depend on the selected trigger Filters Delayed Sending - enable this option to configure when the message is sent after the trigger occurs: Simple Delay - the message is sent after the specified delay Schedule - the message is sent only on the selected days of the week and within the specified time interval When Schedule is selected, specify the days of the week and the time interval during which messages can be sent. If the trigger occurs outside this interval, the message is postponed until the next available time. The schedule follows the timezone selected in the Timezone field in the main details. It is shown in the hint below the schedule. Triggers Triggers Entering a Segment - the mailing is sent when a guest enters one of the segments selected in the Added to segments field. Choose who receives the mailing: Only New Guests - guests who enter the segment after the mailing is started Current And New Guests - right after the start, all guests who are already in the segment, and then guests who enter the segment later If a guest is in several selected segments at once, the mailing is sent to them only once. With delayed sending, the system checks before sending that the guest is still in at least one of the selected segments. If the guest has left them, the message is not sent. For guests who were already in the segment when the mailing was started, the delay and schedule are counted from the moment the mailing is started. The recipient choice cannot be changed in an active mailing. Guest Registration in Loyalty Program - the mailing is sent when a guest registers in the loyalty program. This applies both to new guests and to guests who were already in the system before registering. Creating a guest without registering in the loyalty program does not trigger the mailing. Closed Order - the mailing is sent when the guest's order is closed. timezone If Delayed Sending with Schedule is enabled, select in the Send mailing using field which timezone the schedule follows: Mailing Timezone - the timezone from the main details of the mailing. Trigger Event Timezone - the timezone of the location where the order was closed. This is useful if the locations are in different timezones: for example, with a schedule from 10:00 to 20:00, guests of each location receive the message during these hours in their local time. Bonus Accrual - the mailing is sent when bonuses are accrued to the guest. Bonus Write-off - the mailing is sent when the guest's bonuses are written off. Loyalty Group Change Loyalty Group Change - the mailing is sent when a guest moves from one loyalty group to another. In the From Loyalty Groups field, select the groups the guest must move from, and in the To Loyalty Groups field, the groups the guest must move to. The message is sent if the guest moves from any group in the first field to any group in the second one. The mailing can be set up for a level upgrade or downgrade. For example, to notify a guest about moving to a less favorable group, select the higher groups in the From Loyalty Groups field, for example 5%, 7%, and 10%, and the lower ones in the To Loyalty Groups field, for example 0% and 3%. The same group should not be selected in both fields, otherwise the mailing will be sent both on an upgrade and on a downgrade. The system does not distinguish between an upgrade and a downgrade on its own - it all depends on the selected groups. If a guest skips one or more groups, they receive only one message. For example, when moving straight from 0% to 5%, skipping 3%, the message is sent once - for the move from 0% to 5%. When a guest registers in the loyalty program and receives their first group, the mailing is not sent. See setup examples for mailings with different triggers in Use Cases. Cascade Cascade The Cascade step appears if Cascade is selected in the Mailing Format field. A cascade sends the message to a guest through several channels one after another: if the message could not be delivered through one channel, the system moves on to the next one. This way, you can start with cheaper channels and switch to more expensive ones only when needed, for example Push → E-mail → WhatsApp → SMS. Channels - select at least two channels. While only one channel is selected, you cannot proceed to the Content step Delivery Order - drag the channels into the required order. The channel in the top row is used first The cascade runs separately for each guest: the message is sent through the first channel if the message is delivered, the cascade ends for this guest and the next channels are not used if the message is not delivered - for example, the guest has no contact for this channel or the provider rejected the message - the system sends the message through the next channel if the message is not delivered through any channel, the cascade ends for this guest without delivery Until the sending result for the current channel is known, the system does not move on to the next channel. Delivery attempts through the current channel continue for up to 24 hours. In a draft, the cascade can be configured freely. In an active mailing, the cascade cannot be changed: you cannot add or remove a channel, change the delivery order, or switch between Cascade and One Channel. To do this, pause the mailing, rebuild the cascade, and start it again. All other settings can be changed directly in the active mailing. Content Create Select the sending channel and configure the message content. Available channels: SMS — enter the message text Push — if necessary, specify a title and enter the push notification text E-mail — specify the subject and message text. You can add HTML instead of text. If necessary, attach files. You can specify a name and comment for each attached file WhatsApp - select a template in the Template field. Only templates approved by Meta are available. The message text is taken from the template and cannot be edited in the mailing To personalize the message, you can add variables to the text - see Variables. The result is displayed in the preview. After configuring the content, click Create. The mailing will be saved as a draft. You can start the draft immediately from the mailing page or open it later on the Draft tab. Variables A variable inserts the data of a specific guest into the message, for example their name or discount size. To add a variable, click the button in the lower left corner of the message field and select the required value. In the Preview block, sample values are shown instead of the variables. variables Variables are grouped into blocks: Guest - Greetings, Greetings with name, First name, Last name Location - Name, Address, Phone, Telegram link Loyalty - Discount percent, Amount to next level, Next level discount percent, Bonuses Feedback - Survey Link If the guest is not a member of the loyalty program or is already at the highest level, the Amount to next level value is not inserted. Variable values are inserted when the mailing is triggered for the guest. With delayed sending, the guest may make a purchase before the message is sent, and then the Amount to next level in the message will be out of date. Start Mailing Create To start a saved mailing, go to the Draft tab, open the required mailing, and click Start. In the confirmation window, click Start again. The current changes to the mailing will be saved automatically. After it is started, the mailing moves from Draft to Active and begins working when the specified trigger occurs, taking into account the configured delay, schedule, and sending limits. An active Auto mailing can be opened and edited at any time. Any changes you make apply to subsequent mailing activity. For a WhatsApp mailing, the channel and the template cannot be changed. Pause Pause To stop an Auto mailing, open it and click Pause. In the confirmation window, click Pause again. A mailing can also be paused by the system if segments, filters, locations, or other objects used in its settings have been changed or deleted, making it impossible to send messages. The deleted value is automatically cleared from the mailing settings. The mailing will receive the On pause status. While the mailing is paused, messages are not sent, including those that have already been queued for sending. To view paused mailings, open Filters and select the On pause status. Resume Mailing To resume a mailing, open it and click Activate. In the confirmation window, click Activate again. For the Entering a Segment trigger, choose again who receives the mailing when activating it. If current and new guests are selected, current guests are those who are in the segment at the moment of activation. If the mailing was paused by the system, specify a new value to replace the deleted one before activation, for example, select another segment, and save the changes. The mailing cannot be activated until the missing value is replaced. Use Cases Birthday Gift for Regular Guests There is no separate birthday trigger. To congratulate guests, use a segment with the Birthday condition and the Entering a Segment trigger: In Main Details, select a segment of regular guests in the Segments field - only they will receive the gift. In Conditions, select the Entering a Segment trigger, in the Added to segments field - a segment with the Birthday = today condition, recipients - Current And New Guests. In Content, add the guest name variable to the text. Segments are recalculated once a day. A guest who registered after the recalculation and has a birthday today will enter the segment only at the next recalculation and will not receive the mailing that day. Welcome to the Loyalty Program In Conditions, select the Guest Registration in Loyalty Program trigger. Enable Delayed Sending with Simple Delay, for example 1 hour, so that the message does not arrive right after registration. In Content, explain how to earn and spend bonuses. New Level Congratulations In Conditions, select the Loyalty Group Change trigger. In the To Loyalty Groups field, select the new level, for example 7%, and in the From Loyalty Groups field - all groups below it: 0%, 3%, and 5%. In Content, congratulate the guest and tell them about the new benefits, for example "Your discount is now 7%". One mailing cannot cover all level upgrades: if the same group is selected in both fields, the mailing is also sent on a downgrade. So create a separate mailing for each level. For example, for the groups 0%, 3%, 5%, 7%, and 10%, you need four mailings: New Level 3%: from 0% to 3% New Level 5%: from 0% and 3% to 5% New Level 7%: from 0%, 3%, and 5% to 7% New Level 10%: from 0%, 3%, 5%, and 7% to 10% This way, a guest who skips a level also receives one message - about the group they moved to. Thank You After a Visit In Conditions, select the Closed Order trigger. Enable Delayed Sending with Simple Delay, for example 2 hours. In Content, thank the guest for the visit.

title: Create Guest
text: To create a new guest: Go to Marketing → Guests Click Create Enter the guest details Click Create Create Guest 1\. First Name 2\. Last Name 3\. Sex 4\. Birthday 5\. Email 6\. Telegram 7\. Phone Number/Card Number By default, a guest is identified by their phone number. To use a card number for identification, click Card Number, then enter the card number. If a card number is entered, a phone number cannot be added. Edit Guest To edit a guest, use one of the following methods: Open the guest profile, click the button with the colon icon, and select Edit In the guest table, right-click the required guest and select Edit from the context menu Make the required changes and click Save. Colon Button Phone Numbers A guest profile can contain multiple phone numbers. Phone numbers can be edited, and one of them can be set as the primary number for communication with the guest. The phone number associated with a loyalty card cannot be changed. When a new phone number is added, the system checks whether it is already used in another guest profile. If the number is already in use, a warning will appear. If confirmed, the guest profile that previously used this number will be deactivated. Phone Number Already in Use If a guest changes their phone number and wants to keep their bonus points and loyalty level: Add the new phone number to the guest profile as an additional number Ask the guest to register in the loyalty system using the new number After registration, set the new number as the primary number Bonus points and loyalty level will be automatically synchronized with the new card. If the guest has already registered in the loyalty system using the new number: In this case, a second guest profile may appear in the system. To combine the data into one profile: Open the guest profile with the old phone number Add the new number as an additional number Confirm the deactivation of the second profile in the warning that appears Set the new number as the primary number As a result, only one active guest profile will remain, and the bonus points and loyalty level will be synchronized. Deactivated Guest A guest profile is deactivated if its phone number is added to another profile. In this case, the phone number will be associated with the new profile, and the bonus points and loyalty level will be synchronized with the new card. After deactivation, the profile remains available for viewing, but its data cannot be edited. A deactivated guest is not included in the RFM calculation.

title: Create Location Group
text: To create a Location Group, click Create, fill in the required fields, and click Create. Create Group Name Description Locations — select one or more locations to include in the group. Group Access Type — select the type of access to the guest database: — Full Base — group users get access to the entire guest database of the chain. — Group Base — group users get access only to guests who have activity at locations within this group. Edit Location Group To change the group settings, click the required group in the list. In the window that opens, make the necessary changes and click Save. Delete Location Group To delete a group, right-click it and select Delete. Confirm the deletion in the window that opens. Delete Group

title: Create Manual Mailing
text: A Manual mailing is started by a user and sent to the selected audience once. To create a Manual mailing, go to Marketing → Mailings, select Manual, and click Create. Main Details Create In the first step, configure the main mailing settings: Type Mass — for informational messages not related to sales or service events Marketing — for promotional messages intended to encourage guests to make a purchase Service — for messages related to guest service or a specific service event Mailing Format One Channel - the message is sent through one selected channel Cascade - the message is sent through several channels one after another. If Cascade is selected, the Cascade step appears after the main details, where you select the channels and the delivery order. How a cascade works is described in Create Auto Mailing Extra Priority — enable this option if the mailing should be sent without taking the general limits into account Priority - the share of sending this mailing gets when several mailings are sent at the same time, see Mailings. The priority cannot be changed after the mailing is started. Name Timezone - the timezone used by the delayed sending schedule. Segments Description Filters Delayed Sending - enable this option so that messages are not sent immediately after the start: Simple Delay - sending starts after the specified interval after the mailing is started. Schedule - messages are sent only on the selected days of the week and within the specified time interval. Delayed sending is useful for large mailings that may take several hours to send. When Schedule is selected, messages that were not sent before the end of the allowed interval are sent in the next allowed interval, not at night. The schedule follows the timezone selected in the Timezone field. It is shown in the hint below the schedule. The list of guests matching the selected segments and filters is displayed at the bottom of the page. After changing segments or filters, click Update to refresh the list and the number of guests. Click Next. Content Create In the second step, select the sending channel and configure the message content: SMS — enter the message text Push — if necessary, specify a title and enter the push notification text E-mail — specify the subject and message text. You can add HTML instead of text. If necessary, attach documents WhatsApp - select a template in the Template field. Only templates approved by Meta are available. The message text is taken from the template and cannot be edited in the mailing Variables — if necessary, add guest, location, or loyalty program data to the message. See the list of variables in Create Auto Mailing Preview — check how the message will look for the recipient After configuring the content, click Create. The mailing will be saved as a draft. You can start the draft immediately from the mailing page or open it later on the Draft tab. Start Mailing To start a saved mailing, go to the Draft tab, open the required mailing, and click Start. Before sending, the system builds the recipient list again based on the current segments and filters, so its composition and number may differ from those displayed when the mailing was created. The confirmation window displays the final number of recipients. Click Start. After the mailing is started, its settings can no longer be edited. The mailing moves from Draft to Active and receives the In progress status. If delayed sending is enabled, messages are sent after the specified delay or during the time allowed by the schedule. When all messages receive a final status, the mailing status changes to Finished. The number of delivered messages may differ from the number of sent messages. Create Recipients The mailing page displays: Guests Amount - how many guests receive the mailing Sent - the total number of sending attempts through all channels. In a cascade, if the message was not delivered through the first channel, it is sent to the guest through the next channel, and each attempt is counted. That is why this value can be greater than the number of guests Delivered - how many guests received the message In the screenshot, the mailing was sent as a cascade. The message was not delivered to either guest through the first channel, so the system sent it through the second one. That is why, with two guests, Sent is 4 and Delivered is 2. The Delivery Status column shows the final result for each guest, taking all cascade channels into account. Stop Mailing If a mailing was started with an error, for example the wrong filters were selected, you can stop it. To do this, right-click the mailing row in the list and select Stop. You can also open the mailing itself and click Stop on its page. Only a mailing with the In progress status can be stopped. After it is stopped, the mailing receives the Stopped status: messages that are still waiting to be sent are not sent. For such recipients, the Delivery Status column on the mailing page shows Stopped messages that have already been passed for sending will be sent and may be delivered A stopped mailing cannot be resumed or started again. To send it with corrected settings, duplicate the mailing - right-click the mailing row and select Duplicate, or click the duplicate button on the mailing page. A new mailing with the same settings opens. Make the changes and start it. Guests who have already been sent the original mailing will receive the message again if they are included in the audience of the new mailing. To avoid this, set up limits.

title: Create Metric
text: To add a metric to the Master Chart: 1\. Click Add Metric 2\. Select the required metric parameters 3\. Click Create Add metric The metric appears on the chart and in the legend. New Metric 1\. Custom Metric Name Optional field. The specified name is displayed on the chart instead of the system name. If a name is specified, the metric filters are not shown in the legend. 2\. Category The category determines which metrics and filters are available. Finance Sales Sales by Guests Guest Base 3\. Metric The set of available metrics depends on the selected category. Finance Income Expenses Sales Revenue: Revenue Gross — sales amount before discounts Revenue Net — sales amount after discounts Cost and profit: Profit Gross — the difference between revenue and cost of goods sold Cost of Goods Sold — calculated based on the dish composition from recipe cards and ingredient costs from iiko Discounts: Discount Total Discount Loyalty Discount Bonuses — the amount of bonuses used. Bonuses are not included in Discount Total Orders and guests: Order Count Guest Count — the total number of guests specified in orders. One order can be for several guests, so the metric value can exceed the order count Average check: Avg Check Per Order Avg Check Per Guest Avg Check Per Order Per Hour — the ratio of revenue to the total duration of orders Avg Check Per Guest Per Hour — shows how much revenue, on average, falls on one guest for one hour of order duration Sales by Guests Metrics in this category are calculated based on sales data linked to guests. Revenue: Revenue Net Avg Revenue per Unique Guest — the ratio of revenue to the number of unique guests Discounts: Discount Total Discount Loyalty Discount Bonuses — the amount of bonuses used. Bonuses are not included in Discount Total Orders and guests: Order Count Unique Guests — each identified guest is counted once regardless of the number of their orders. Each order without a linked guest is counted as a separate guest. Average check: Avg Check Per Order Avg Check Per Order Per Hour — the ratio of revenue to the total duration of orders Frequency and behavior: Avg Orders per Unique Guest — the ratio of the order count to the number of unique guests Avg Duration — the average duration of an order Guest Base Guest Base — the total number of unique guests accumulated by a certain date. The base includes guests who have at least one order or reservation in the selected locations. 4\. Segment Available for the Sales by Guests and Guest Base categories. By default, the metric is calculated for All Guests. To calculate it for a specific group of guests, select a custom segment. You can use static and dynamic segments created in the Guest Segments section. The metric is calculated using the current segment composition as of its last update, not the composition for the selected period. If the segment is deleted, the metric is calculated for All Guests. 5\. Display Settings The set of available display settings depends on the selected metric. ABS / % — displays the metric as an absolute value or as a percentage. When % is selected, specify the value the percentage is calculated from. For example, for the Revenue Net metric you can select Of Revenue Gross. Accumulated — values are summed up sequentially from the beginning of the selected period. "Accumulated" is added to the metric name in the legend. Space — recalculates the metric value per Area (per m²) or per Seats. The area is taken from the location settings, and the number of seats from the floor plan. If several locations are selected, the metric value is calculated relative to their total area or total number of seats. Accumulated and Space cannot be used at the same time. Chart Type — bar or line. The chart type is set separately for each metric, so both types can be used on the same chart. Color — the color of the metric on the chart Metric Filters Filters allow you to include only part of the data in a metric, for example, revenue only for the evening or only for card payments. Filters The set of available filters depends on the selected category and metric. Filters apply only to the metric being created and do not affect the other metrics on the Master Chart. After selecting the values, click Apply. Edit Metric Click the metric name in the Master Chart legend to open its settings. Change the required parameters and click Save. Duplicate Metric In the metric settings, click the duplicate icon. The form for creating a new metric opens with the parameters of the original metric. Change the required parameters and click Create. A metric with completely identical settings cannot be added to the same chart. Delete Metric In the metric settings, click Delete Metric.
description: How to add a metric to the Master Chart: categories, metrics, display settings, and filters.

title: Create Template
text: To create a template, go to Marketing → Mailings, click Templates, then Create. Template Text create Fill in the fields: Name - used to select the template in a mailing. The name must be unique: two templates with the same name cannot be created, even if their languages differ Language - RU or EN. The language is sent for approval together with the template. The text is not translated automatically Message text - if necessary, add variables: guest, location, or loyalty program data. To add a variable, click the button in the message field and select the required value The Preview block shows a sample message with the variable values filled in. variables Variables are grouped into blocks: Guest - Greetings, Greetings with name, First name, Last name Location - Name, Address, Phone, Telegram link Loyalty - Discount percent, Amount to next level, Next level discount percent Feedback - Survey Link If the guest is not a member of the loyalty program or is already at the highest level, the Amount to next level value is not inserted. Buttons create You can add up to two buttons to a template. Buttons are optional: a template can contain text only. To add a button, click Add Button and select the type: Link - opens a web page. Enter the Button Text and the full page address in the URL field Phone - opens the dialer for a regular phone call, not a WhatsApp call. Enter the Button Text, select the country code, and enter the Phone Number Button specifics: Only one phone button is allowed. One or two links, one phone, or a link and a phone are possible Button text - up to 20 characters Variables are not supported in buttons: the button text, link, and phone number are the same for all recipients Buttons appear in the message in the order they were added. Their order cannot be changed Sending for Approval Click Create & Send to approval. The template is created and immediately sent for approval to Meta. In the template list, it gets the On Approval status. A template cannot be changed after it is created. If you need to adjust the text or buttons, create a copy of the template - for details, see Templates. Once the template gets the Approved status, it can be selected in a WhatsApp mailing: Create Auto Mailing Create Manual Mailing

title: Creating a Reservation
text: Methods of Creating a Reservation You can create a reservation in three ways. This helps you choose the most convenient option depending on the situation and speeds up work with the functionality. reserv-create-options 1\. Selecting a Time Interval on the Timeline Find a suitable time and table on the timeline. Hover over the timeline cell - a + appears in it. A single click will open the sidebar to set up the reservation. Click and drag right or left will immediately set the required reservation duration. Dragging up or down will allow you to select multiple tables. In the opened sidebar specify the guest. Add tables or if necessary change the selected table. If necessary, edit the interval or reservation date. Fill in the remaining fields — number of guests, comment, reservation source, tags. Disable or keep SMS notification about the reservation. To save the reservation click Save. 2\. Quick Reservation for Walk-in Guests The button with a walking person icon above the + button creates a quick reservation for guests who came without a reservation. Select the number of guests and click Create - the reservation is created with the Started status, and a table is selected automatically. 3\. Button + Click the + button in the lower right corner of the timeline. In the opened sidebar specify the guest. If necessary, select one or more tables. If necessary, edit the interval or reservation date. Fill in the remaining fields — number of guests, comment, reservation source, tags. Disable or keep SMS notification about the reservation. To save the reservation click Save. Sidebar When you select any of the methods, a sidebar opens. It is here that all information about the reservation is filled in. In the panel you can add or change a guest, select or change a table, specify an interval, number of guests, add a comment and see the reservation change history. The reservation source, status and SMS sending parameters are also indicated there. To create a reservation, it is enough to specify a guest, the remaining fields will be filled in by default. 1\. Guest When you click on a guest, a second sidebar opens. In it, you can find a guest, leave the reservation without a specific guest, or create a new one. reserv-guest1 Find a guest by phone number, name or loyalty card and add them to the reservation. Do not add a specific guest - select Walk-in Guest or click the ghost icon next to the guest field. A Guest name field appears below the guest field - fill it in to address the guest by name, or leave it empty. No new guest is created in the database. Create a new guest and add them to the reservation. Creating a Guest To create a new guest, you need to specify the following data: Name (Last name is not required) Phone number Gender More about creating a guest can be read in the article Create Guest. 2\. Table Selection {#multireserve} You can select one or more tables for a reservation. Assigning a table right away is optional — a reservation can be saved without a table and the table can be selected later. If several tables are selected for one reservation, it is considered a multi-reservation. In a multi-reservation, tables must be occupied continuously: there must be no gaps between the reservation times of different tables. More about multi-reservations can be read in the article Multi-Table Reservation. To select multiple tables: In the sidebar, enable Select multiple tables. Find the required tables in the list. You can use search by name, filters and sorting. Select the tables and click Apply. Reservation without a table. If it is not yet clear at the time of creating the reservation which table to seat the guest at, the table can be selected later. A reservation without an assigned table is displayed in a separate No Table sidebar until a table is assigned. 3\. Reservation Date and Start Time Start time is a multiple of 15-minute intervals. By default, when creating a reservation by button, the nearest time that is a multiple of 15 minutes is specified. For example, it is now 18:12, when creating a reservation, time 18:15 will be specified. 4\. Duration Reservation duration is also a multiple of 15 minutes. By default, when creating using the +Add Reservation button, 2 hours is specified. 5\. Number of Guests You can quickly specify up to 10 guests, or manually specify a larger company. By default, one guest is specified. To specify a company of more than 10 people, click 10+ and enter the required number manually. 6\. Reservation Source The field is required; the default source of the location is selected automatically. Specifying the reservation source will allow you to then analyze where guest reservations come from. This helps you understand which channels work better and which ones work worse, so you can evaluate their effectiveness and optimize guest acquisition. The list shows the sources enabled in the location settings, including custom sources. Reservation Source Learn more about setting up the list of sources in the Reservation Sources article. 7\. Reservation Tags Reservation tags help you manually mark reservations. With their help you can visually highlight important records, quickly understand the context of a reservation, group reservations and find them using filters. More about creating and using tags can be read in the article Reservation Tags. 8\. Comment In the comment you can specify any necessary information about the reservation. 9\. Reservation Status It shows whether the reservation is confirmed or if the guest cancelled it. You can select it only manually in the sidebar when creating or editing a reservation. Three statuses are available when creating a reservation: Confirmed (Selected by default when creating a reservation for today) Not confirmed (Selected by default when creating a reservation for a future date) In progress There are a total of five statuses for reservations. More about statuses can be read in the article Reservation Statuses. 10\. SMS Notification If a reservation is created for the future, after selecting a guest you can choose to send an SMS notification. The SMS template is configured separately in the Reservations - Settings section. By default, this option is active. Read further: — Automatic check creation from reservation
description: How to create a reservation. Description of fields

title: Creating a Reservation
text: To create a reservation, tap + at the top of the reservation list. The new reservation form opens. Create Reservation Button Creating a Reservation Form Fields Don't Change - prevents changing the table and the guest in the reservation. All other fields can be changed. Select Guest - search for a guest or create a new one. If no specific guest is needed, tap the ghost icon button on the right - the reservation will show Walk-in Guest without a name and phone number. Select Table - one or several tables. A reservation can be saved without a table, and the table can be selected later. Date - use the arrows to go to the previous or next day, or select a date with the calendar icon. Time and Duration - changed with the - and + buttons in 15-minute steps. Reservation Interval below shows the start and end time of the reservation. Number of guests - up to 10 guests are selected by tapping the icon; for a larger party tap 10+ and enter the number manually. Reservation source Comment Status - Confirmed by default. If reservation tags are used in the establishment, the form also has a field for reservation tags. To save the reservation, tap Create.
description: How to create a reservation in the CosmosResto Reservations app on the phone.

title: Creating and Configuring a Survey
text: The builder allows you to assemble a survey from pages and questions, configure the completion scenario and design the form for the respondent. To create a draft, you must fill in the required fields of the basic information and add at least one question. Creating a Survey Open the Surveys section. Click Create. On the Details step, specify the name and location. On the Questions step, configure the survey structure. If necessary, configure transitions between survey stages on the Conditions step. If necessary, change the appearance on the Design step. Click Create on the last step. After a successful save, the system will create a survey with the status Draft. The Distribution section will become available on the survey page, and the Save button will replace the Create button. Step 1. Details Name Location Step 2. Questions At this step, the survey structure is formed. You can add, delete and duplicate pages and questions, as well as change their order. Page Types Page with questions Use a page with questions to collect answers. One page can contain one or more questions, and all its content is displayed to the respondent at once. Start screen The start screen is displayed before the questions and there can only be one. It can be used for a welcome message, explaining the purpose of the survey, or obtaining consent for the processing of personal data. On the start screen, you can add text and variables, add an image, enable consent for the processing of personal data, and add the ability to unsubscribe from survey mailings. Information screen An information screen can be placed between pages with questions. It does not require a response and is suitable for instructions, explanations or visual inserts. You can add text, variables and an image to the screen. Final screen The final screen completes the completion scenario. A survey can have several final screens, for example for different branches of the scenario. On the final screen, you can add text, variables, an image and the ability to unsubscribe from survey mailings. If a survey has several final screens and transition conditions are not configured, the respondent is shown the first final screen in order. Consent for Processing of Personal Data This setting is only available on the start screen. Enable Consent to continue. Specify a link to the privacy policy. Save the changes. The respondent will see a required consent checkbox. Until the checkbox is checked, the Start button will be unavailable. Unsubscribing from Survey Mailings This setting can be added to the start or final screen. After confirming the unsubscription, the guest is excluded from further survey mailings. For respondents who opened the survey via an anonymous link, this block is not displayed. If the survey is opened via a public anonymous link, personal variables are not displayed. You can add and manage the order of survey pages at the top of the form. Click on the 2 dots on the page type, or drag manually by holding the 6 dots on the page type. General Question Settings The following basic parameters are available for questions: Question type — determines the answer format: Rating, NPS, Choice or Input. Required — if enabled, the respondent will not be able to continue or submit the survey without an answer. This setting is enabled by default. Question text — a required field. Explanation — additional text under the question. Rating The Rating type is used for a quantitative assessment of the visit, service or another indicator. Available settings: Display type — Stars or Numbers. Scale — 5-point scale (default) or 10-point scale. Include in guest statistics — allows the rating to be used in auto-tag conditions and is included in guest statistics. The setting is available only for the 5-point scale. If a response has several Rating type questions with the guest statistics setting enabled, the system uses the average value of these ratings for this response. NPS The NPS type is used to assess a guest's willingness to recommend the establishment. It is rated on a scale from 1 to 10. Choice The Choice type allows you to offer the respondent ready-made answer options. Available settings: Choice type — Single or multiple choice. Answer options Other answer — adds an option, upon selection of which the respondent enters their own text. For the custom option, you can change the name and configure the requirement and length of the entered text. Input The Input type is used for text responses and contact data. Within one question, you can add several fields, for example name, phone and comment. All filled-in fields are saved as one answer to the question. Available for each field: Title Required Mask — determines the format and validation rules for the entered value. Available masks: Text, First name, Last name, Phone, Email, Number, Date (in DD.MM.YYYY format). Step 3. Conditions Conditions allow you to change the sequential completion of the survey and direct the respondent to different pages depending on the answer. If conditions are not configured, pages are shown sequentially. How to Configure a Transition Open the Conditions step. Find the required question. Click Add condition. Select the respondent's behavior. Select the target page in the Transition field. If necessary, add other conditions. Available conditions: On answer selection — works for Rating, NPS and Choice questions. Specify one or more values for which the transition should occur. Always — the transition occurs regardless of the answer. On skip — triggers if the respondent did not answer. Only available for a non-required question. A transition can only be configured forward: the target page must be located after the current one. This eliminates scenario looping. If several conditions are configured for a question, the system checks them from top to bottom and executes the first matching condition. When changing the structure, take the following into account: If you move the target page before the current one, the transition will become invalid and will need to be reconfigured; If you make a question required, the On skip condition for it will be reset; When a page is deleted, transitions to it are cleared; When a question is deleted, conditions related to it are deleted. Step 4. Design The Design section changes only the appearance of the web form and does not affect the survey completion logic. The form automatically adapts to mobile devices and computers. The width of the content is determined by the system. Available settings: Color of background, fields, buttons, accent elements and text; Logo; Link that redirects when the logo is clicked; Background image; Background image darkening.
description: Creating a survey, configuring questions, screens, transition conditions and appearance.

title: Editing and Canceling a Reservation
text: You can edit a reservation in several ways: through the sidebar, timeline, floor plan or reservations table. Through the Sidebar Click on a reservation on the timeline. In the opened sidebar make changes: guest, table, date and time, number of guests, tags, comment, status. Click Save to apply the changes. The sidebar also has Reservation Change Log. Using the Timeline Select a reservation on the timeline. Click and hold the reservation again. Drag the reservation to another table or another time. If necessary, add an additional table by selecting it on the timeline. Click Save to apply the changes. In the Floor Plan Section Select a reservation in the left sidebar (for convenience you can filter the list by table by selecting it on the floor plan). If necessary, select a table on the floor plan to show only its reservations. In the opened sidebar make changes: guest, table, date and time, number of guests, tags, comment, status. Click Save to apply the changes. By selecting a table with an In progress reservation on the floor plan, you can quickly change the status or edit the reservation time by 15 minutes. In the Reservations Table Click on a reservation in the list. In the opened sidebar make changes: guest, table, date and time, number of guests, tags, comment, status. Click Save to apply the changes. Editing Multi-Reservations In a multi-reservation you can: Edit all tables simultaneously. Edit individual tables independently. To exclude a table from editing, click on it. 1\. If All Tables Are Selected: Increasing or decreasing time on one slot will affect all associated tables. The sidebar allows editing of guest, date and time, number of guests, tags, comment, status. It is possible to add additional tables by selecting them on the timeline or specifying through the sidebar. Editing time of a multi-reservation through the sidebar is only available if the start and end times are the same for all tables. 2\. If One Table Is Selected: Increase or decrease time on this table, remembering the limitations. In the sidebar, start time and duration can be edited for each individual table. Even if only one table is selected, changing the guest, number of guests, tags, comment or status changes apply to the entire reservation. Blocking Reservation Changes Blocking prohibits changing guest and table. Any user can remove the block at any time. To block a reservation: Click Do not change. After blocking, hover over the button to see the blocking time and the user who set the block. Canceling a Reservation To cancel a reservation: Set status to Cancelled. Select the reason for cancellation. After cancellation, the reservation is automatically moved to the Archive section. Read further: — Reservation Statuses
description: Capabilities when editing a reservation.

title: Editing and Managing a Survey
text: Editing a Survey Surveys with the statuses Draft, Published and Unpublished can be edited if you have the appropriate permissions. A deactivated survey is available for viewing only. Restrictions After Receiving Responses If the survey has no responses yet, the structure can be edited without restrictions. If at least one response has been received, some parameters are locked so as not to change the type of already saved data. Changes to a published survey apply to new completions, including via previously sent links. Already received responses are retained. After receiving responses, you cannot change: The question type; The field mask in an Input type question; The choice type Single or Multiple in a Choice type question. Open the survey. Change the necessary parameters. Click Save. If the survey is published, confirm the change to the published form. Text changes are not stored as a separate historical version: current names of questions, fields and options are displayed in old responses. When a new field or option is added, it is not present in old responses, and deleted elements are retained in those responses where they had already been filled in. Duplicating a Survey When duplicating, the system creates a new survey with the status Draft and copies the basic information, questions and pages, transition conditions and design settings. Publication settings and responses are not copied. To duplicate a survey: Open the context menu of the required survey by right-clicking on the required survey in the list. Or open the survey page. Select the duplication action. The system will open the creation form and fill it with data from the original survey. Make the necessary changes. Click Save. Deactivating and Deleting a Survey Deactivation is used if a previously published survey should no longer be returned to use. You can deactivate a survey with the status Published or Unpublished. Deletion is available for a survey with the status Draft. After confirmation, the draft is deleted from the list. To Deactivate/Delete a survey: Open the context menu of the required survey by right-clicking on the required survey in the list. Or open the survey page. Select the action Delete or Deactivate. Confirm the action. For previously published surveys, use unpublishing or deactivation depending on whether you plan to return the survey to use. After deactivation: The status changes to Deactivated; Links become unavailable; The survey cannot be connected to a mailing; The survey opens only in view mode; editing and republishing are unavailable. Deactivation is irreversible. Use unpublishing for a temporary stop.
description: Editing, deactivating, deleting and duplicating a survey.

title: Exporting Responses
text: Export allows you to download survey results for additional analysis in spreadsheets or BI systems. Data can be exported from the responses of a specific survey or from the general Responses table. General Export Rules When exporting, the system takes into account the current view of the table. The columns exported are those selected in the column display settings, and their order. The applied sorting and active filters are taken into account. The Text Responses and Ratings columns are used only in the table interface and are not included in the export. Instead, the system exports detailed answers to the questions. The detailed block always preserves the structure of the survey questions. If a question was not shown to the respondent due to conditions, or the answer is missing, the corresponding value remains empty. Exporting Responses for a Single Survey Open a survey from the list of surveys Click View responses Click the export button If the export is performed from the Responses tab of a specific survey: Each question is exported into a separate column; The column name becomes the text of the question; Questions are arranged in the same order as in the survey; Values for each question are filled in the response row. This format is convenient to use when you need to compare respondents' answers to the same set of questions. Exporting the General Responses Table Open the section Feedback -> Responses Set filtering and other table parameters Click the export button If the export is performed from the general Responses table: The survey name is added to the export; Questions and answers are output through the Question and Answer fields; The export takes into account the selected filters by period, locations, surveys and other parameters. This option is suitable for analyzing data across several surveys at once. Response Format by Question Type Rating and NPS — a numeric value is exported. Input — the entered text is exported. If a question has several fields, their values are saved together. For specialized fields, for example first name, last name or phone number, the field name and the entered value are specified. Choice — the selected options are exported. If the respondent used Custom option, its text is also included in the value. Deleted responses are not included in the export.
description: Rules for exporting responses for a single survey and from the general Responses table.

title: Floor Plan
text: Floor plan is a visual representation of the establishment's tables, which allows you to assess the hall occupancy and manage reservations tied to specific tables. The section displays the status of tables for the selected date and time. The color and additional information on the table depend on the reservation status and the selected display mode. The state of the plan depends on the selected time. When switching time slots, the system updates the statuses of tables and information about related reservations. By default, the sidebar displays a list of all reservations and their statuses from all tables at the current time. Main elements: Table plan — shows the location of tables, their capacity and current state. Reservations sidebar — displays reservations of the selected table or a general list of reservations. Time panel — determines the status of tables at the selected moment. Button to create a reservation Floor or zone selection — switches the displayed part of the establishment. Display settings — configures the information in tooltips next to tables and plan display. Each table displays: Number or name; Maximum capacity; Deposit indicator, if any. How the floor plan takes into account the selected time The time panel is divided into 15-minute intervals. The minimum reservation duration is 15 minutes and must be a multiple of 15 minutes. The selected time affects: The color and state of tables; Information in the placards next to tables; Selection of reservations for editing; Start time when creating a reservation. Clicking on a table filters the list of reservations in the left sidebar only by the selected table. Table States Color designations of table status are similar to the general status model with some additions. Main statuses on the floor plan: Yellow — in status "Confirmed" Orange — in status "Not confirmed" Green — in status "In progress" Pink — in status "Not confirmed", if guest is late Light blue — in status "Confirmed", if guest is late Unique display for floor plan: Table is free Table lock Collision - intersection with an existing reservation on this table Viewing reservations of the selected table Select a date and time. Click on the required table. The sidebar will show a list of reservations for this table for the selected day. Select a reservation card to view detailed information and available actions. Reservations in the sidebar are grouped by statuses. A started reservation is displayed first. Quick actions are available for a started reservation: Change the duration of the reservation −15 minutes — decrease duration +15 minutes — increase duration Change reservation status - click on the status dropdown list to select Move guests - open menu to transfer the reservation to another table. Read more about moving below in this article. The name of the selected table is displayed at the top of the sidebar. Click on it to open information about the table, including its blocking periods for the selected day. To return to the general list of reservations, click on a free area of the plan or deselect the table. Guest Information When you hover over a placard with the guest's name, you can see additional information about the guest. The tooltip displays 5 tags. The full list of tags is available in the guest profile. Configuring the Display of Information About Tables The display panel controls the content of information placards next to tables. The following modes are available: Guest — first and last name of the guest of the current reservation. If there is no current reservation, the placard is not displayed. Reservations — up to three reservations: current and two next or three next. Past reservations are not displayed in the placard. Time shows: Time until the end of the current reservation Time until the start of the next reservation, if there is no current one Time overdue after the start of an unconfirmed or confirmed reservation, if guests have not yet arrived. Money — the amount of the current reservation's check. Waiter — name and last name of the waiter from the current reservation's check. If there is no data for the selected mode, the placard next to the table is not displayed. Configuring Objects on the Plan In the plan settings you can hide or show additional objects. Constructions - walls, windows, doors, stairs. Interior - speakers, televisions, outlets, text labels and chair display. Details - when activated, optimizes this section for devices with low performance or low internet speed. Changes are applied immediately after switching the setting and are saved after page reload. After fully logging out of the account, settings may be reset. Creating a Reservation You can create a reservation on the floor plan in several ways: Click the + button after selecting a time; Select a table and click the + button; Open the context menu of the table (right-click) and select Create reservation. Creating a Reservation Select time on the scale. Click +. The selected table will be automatically entered in the form. Fill in the reservation form. All fields for creating a reservation are described in more detail in this article. If necessary, select a table. If the table was not selected, suitable tables for the specified time will be highlighted on the floor plan. Check the duration and other reservation fields. Save the changes. Clicking on a table does not create a reservation. It opens a list of reservations for the selected table. Overlapping Reservations The system can save multiple reservations for one table at overlapping times. Such an overlap is called a collision. When creating or changing a reservation, the system warns of an overlap, but does not block saving. A collision is displayed on the table with a separate visual state. The number of overlapping reservations on one table is not limited. A reservation can also be saved over a table block. Before saving, check the time and selected table. A collision means that multiple reservations claim the same table at the same time period. Editing a Reservation Select the reservation you are interested in from the sidebar (for convenience, you can filter the list by table by selecting it on the floor plan). Change the necessary parameters. Save the changes. Editing is performed in the standard reservation form. In it you can change the time, duration, table and other available parameters. More about editing reservations can be read in this article. Moving Guests {#replace} For a started reservation, you can move guests to another table. Click Move in the card of the started reservation or right-click on the table with the required reservation at this moment. Select the move action. Specify a full transfer of the reservation or a transfer from a specific time. Select a new table. Check the preview result and possible overlaps. Confirm the move. If there are associated checks, the system initiates their transfer to the new table.
description: Navigation and functionality of the Floor Plan

title: Floor Plan
text: To open the floor plan, tap Menu at the top of the screen and select the floor plan. The plan shows the tables of the floor and their state for the selected date and time. Floor Plan Screen Elements Date - use the arrows to go to the previous or next day. Zoom to fit - fits the floor plan to the screen. The plan can be zoomed and moved with your fingers. Floor - the floor name and the number of occupied tables out of all tables, for example First Floor 5 / 18. If there are several floors, they are shown next to each other, each with its own number of occupied tables. Time scale at the bottom of the screen - time selection in 15-minute steps. The current time is highlighted with a frame. The state of the tables on the plan depends on the selected time. Table Colors The table color depends on the reservation status at the selected time: Yellow - status Confirmed; Orange - status Not Confirmed; Green - status Started; Pink - status Not Confirmed, if the guest is late; Light blue - status Confirmed, if the guest is late. A grey table is free. Display Settings The buttons above the time scale select which info is shown in the label next to a table: Display Settings Guest - first and last name of the guest of the current reservation. Reservations - up to three reservations: the current one and the next two, or the next three. Time - time until the end of the current reservation, until the start of the next one, or how late the guest is. Money - the check amount of the current reservation. Waiter - first and last name of the waiter from the current reservation's check. If there is no data for the selected mode, the label next to the table is not shown. Reservation for a Table Tap a table on the plan - a window with the list of this table's reservations opens. To create a reservation for this table, tap + Create Reservation. The reservation form opens and is filled in the same way as when creating a reservation from the list - see the Creating a Reservation article.
description: The floor plan in the CosmosResto Reservations app on the phone.

title: General Information
text: Manual Tags allow you to manually mark guests and store information that should be taken into account when providing service. For example, they can be used to identify VIP guests, dietary restrictions, preferences, or special service requirements. Manual Tags are used in several sections of the system: ✔ Reservations — tags can be displayed in the guest profile, on the reservation timeline, and on the floor plan tables, depending on the group settings. If editing is enabled, tags can be assigned and removed directly from a reservation ✔ Guests — tags are displayed in the guest list and guest profile, where they can be assigned and removed ✔ Waiter App — tags can be viewed and assigned to guests if this is allowed in the group settings ✔ Guest Segments — tags are used as one of the filters when creating segments Manual Tag Group List The Manual Tag Group List displays the created groups and their main parameters. To find a group, use the search bar at the top of the page. The search is performed by group name. Manual Tag Group List Table Settings Column Wizard By default, the following columns are displayed in the table: Name — the name of the manual tag group Locations — the locations linked to the group Tags — the tags included in the group Reservations Display — the elements of the Reservations interface where the group tags are displayed Editable in Reservations — indicates whether the group tags can be added or removed in Reservations Available in Waiter App — indicates whether the tag group is available in the Waiter App and whether it can be viewed or edited there Available in Reservation Widget — indicates whether the tag group is available in the Reservation Widget. If enabled, the group's Public Name is displayed in the column; if no Public Name is specified, the group name is used instead Description — the description of the manual tag group Click Table Settings to change the displayed columns. You can also enable the following columns: Author — the employee who created the group, including their name, role, and grade Created At — the date and time when the group was created Last Update — the employee who last updated the group and the date and time of the update Note. Table settings are saved after the page is refreshed. The settings are reset after you log out. Data Filtering Filter To quickly find the required group, use the search bar and filters above the table. Filtering is available by the following parameters: ✔ Author ✔ Created At ✔ Available in Waiter App ✔ Reservations Display ✔ Last Update ✔ Editable in Reservations Note. Filter settings are saved after the page is refreshed. The settings are reset after you log out.

title: General Information
text: What RFM is used for RFM automatically groups guests based on their activity and value to the business. This helps you quickly identify the most loyal guests, those who are beginning to lose interest, and those who need to be re-engaged. Assigned RFM Statuses can be used when working with the guest database, analyzing the audience, and building marketing scenarios. RFM is calculated based on three metrics: ✔ Recency (R) — Number Of Days Since The Last Purchase ✔ Frequency (F) — Average Number Of Checks Per Month Over A Six-Month Period ✔ Monetary (M) — Guest Rating Based On The Amount Spent RFM List Each guest is automatically assigned an RFM Status according to the configured segmentation rules. The status determines which category the guest belongs to based on their visit and spending history. In addition to the RFM Status, an RFM Score is calculated for the most valuable guests. It shows the guest's position among guests with the highest metrics and helps identify the most valuable guests within RFM segments. The score is calculated only for the top 1,000 guests. All other guests are assigned only an RFM Status. RFM is recalculated automatically once a day. It is also recalculated after an RFM Status is created, changed, or deleted. Where RFM is displayed Guest List Guest Profile Reservation List RFM information is displayed in several sections of the system: ✔ Marketing → Guests — the current RFM Status is displayed under each guest's name. ✔ Marketing → Guests — click the required guest and hover over their avatar to view the current RFM Status, RFM Score (if calculated), and status description. ✔ Reservations → Reservation List — RFM is displayed under the guest's name. System Statuses System Statuses The system includes two system RFM Statuses that are created automatically. ✔ No Orders — guests who have not yet had any visits or checks. ✔ Unsorted — guests who have had at least one visit but do not meet the conditions of any configured RFM Status. Deactivated guests are also automatically assigned this status. System Status rows are not interactive and cannot be changed or deleted.

title: General Information
text: A reservation widget is a form on the venue website where guests submit reservation requests themselves. Requests from the widget arrive in the system; how to process them is described in Reservation Requests. To work with widgets, open Reservations → Widgets. Here you can create a widget, configure its appearance and form fields, check the result in the preview and get the code for the website. A widget can be prepared and placed on the website in advance. Requests to a location start arriving only after online reservations from the widget are enabled for that location. Widget List The table shows all created widgets. By default, the list is sorted by creation date: newest widgets first. Widgets Geo — selects the locations whose widgets are shown in the list. Search — search for a widget by name. Filters — filter widgets by conditions. Create — create a new widget. To open a widget for viewing and editing, click its row. Table Settings To change the set of displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ Select the columns to display ✔ Change the column order — drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name ✔ Pin the required columns — click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table ✔ Restore the default settings using Reset to Default Table Settings By default, the table shows the following columns: Created At Name Locations Author Last Update Description Filters Applied filters are displayed above the table next to the Filters button.
