title: Guest List
text: The Guests page displays a list of guests and detailed information about each of them. This page combines guest profiles, visit history, loyalty program data, tags, and other guest information in a single table. By combining search, filters, and table column settings, you can quickly create guest selections and display only the data needed for a specific task. For example, you can find guests with specific tags, analyze their spending and visit history, check loyalty program information, or identify guests whose favorite location matches the selected locations or location groups. Guest List Location Selection In the location selector, you can select an individual location, a location group, or All. Location and Filter Selecting a location or group does not change the list of guests in the table. It determines which locations are used to display statistics for each guest. If a guest has activity at the selected location, the table displays their metrics for that location, such as the last visit and total amount spent. If there was no activity at the selected location, dashes are displayed in the corresponding columns. The selected location is also taken into account when filtering the list. For example, if you select a specific location and set a filter for the amount spent, the table will show guests whose spending at that location meets the specified condition. For more information about location groups, see Location Groups. Search To find a guest, use the search bar above the table. You can search by first name, last name, primary phone number, email, or loyalty card number. Table Settings To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ select the columns to display ✔ change the column order — drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name ✔ pin the required columns — click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table ✔ restore the default settings using Reset to Default Column Settings By default, the following columns are displayed in the table: RFM Score — the guest's numerical score based on the RFM model Guest — the guest's avatar, first name, last name, and current RFM status. Hover over the guest to see their RFM score, a brief description of the current status, and a list of RFM statuses with the percentage of guests in each. The guest's current status is highlighted in the list Phone E-mail Tags — the guest's statuses, autotags, and manual tags. System-assigned statuses are displayed first, followed by autotags and then manual tags Last Visit Total Paid — the total amount spent by the guest across all locations, including payments made in cash, by card, and with bonuses Bonuses Spent — the number of bonuses spent on orders Last Check Avg Check Loyalty Number Loyalty Discount — the guest's current loyalty program discount Loyalty Bonuses — the number of bonuses in the guest's balance You can also enable the following columns. Their position in the table follows the column order in the table settings: Gender — the guest's gender Birthday — the guest's date of birth and age Marketing Consent — consent is enabled by default Survey Consent — consent is enabled by default Favorite Location — the location where the guest has the highest number of checks. If several locations have the same number of checks, the location from the most recent check is displayed Checks — the total number of the guest's checks Avg Check Per Hour — the guest's average spending per hour. Only checks with a visit duration of at least 30 minutes and an amount of at least 1000 are included in the calculation Avg Time — the guest's average visit duration Discount — the total amount of discounts received by the guest Loyalty Total Spent — the guest's cumulative spending in the loyalty program since registration, so it may differ from Total Paid. If the guest is not registered in the loyalty program, no value is displayed Created At — the date when the guest profile was created Loyalty Registration — the date when the guest's loyalty card was registered Source — the guest acquisition source. When registering for the loyalty program, the guest selects the source. For guests created manually in Guests, COSMOS is assigned automatically, while guests created through the reservation system are assigned TIS Notes — notes added to the guest profile Note. Table settings are saved after the page is refreshed. The settings are reset after you log out. Filters If necessary, click Filters to set additional filtering conditions. Guest Filters The following filters are available: Loyalty Total Spent Created At Loyalty Registration Date Marketing Consent Survey Consent Tags Autotags Status Blacklist RFM Status Age Avg Check Avg Check Per Hour Avg Time Birthday Bonuses Spent Checks Discount Favorite Location Gender Last Check Last Visit Loyalty Bonuses Loyalty Group Notes Source Total Paid After selecting the required values, click Apply. Applied filters are displayed above the table. To remove an individual filter, click × next to its name. To reset all filters, click Clear Filters. Note. Filter settings are saved after the page is refreshed. The settings are reset after you log out.

title: Guest List
text: Guest List is a table view of the reservation module that shows guests who have reservations on the selected date. Unlike the timeline, the floor plan and the reservation list, here one row is one guest, even if the guest has several reservations. The guest list helps you: prepare for guest visits; quickly find information about a guest; assess guest activity for the selected day. To open the list, click the guest icon in the left menu of the reservation module. Guest List Page Elements Page Elements Location and date — the list shows guests who have reservations at the selected location on the selected date. Search — by the guest's first name, last name, phone number and loyalty card number. Filters Reservation Status — a quick filter by reservation status. Last Update — the time of the last data update and the refresh button. By default, the table is sorted by the Reservation Period column — from later reservations to earlier ones. Reservation Status Click Reservation Status, check the required statuses and click Apply. The list will show only the guests who have reservations in the selected statuses. Reservation Status By default, the Not Confirmed, Confirmed, Started and Ended statuses are selected. To see guests with cancelled reservations or guests on the waitlist, check the Cancelled and Waitlist statuses. Statistics Statistics on guests and reservations for the selected day are displayed in the lower-right corner of the table. They have two tabs: Active and Cancelled. Statistics On the Active tab, the total number and the number in each status are displayed for guests and reservations: Waitlist, Not Confirmed, Confirmed, Started, Ended. On the Cancelled tab, the data is grouped by cancellation reason. The Guests row shows the number of guests in the reservations, while the Reservations row shows the number of reservations. Table Settings To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ Select the columns to display ✔ Change the column order — drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name ✔ Pin the required columns — click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table ✔ Restore the default settings using Reset to Default Table Settings By default, the table displays the following columns: Guest — the guest's name and RFM segment Phone Loyalty Number Loyalty Discount — the guest's discount under the loyalty program Tags — guest tags Notes — guest notes Reservation Status — the status of the guest's nearest reservation that matches the filters Reservation Period — the start and end time of this reservation Tables Guest Amount Reservation Tags — for more information, read the article Reservation Tags Reservation Comment Guest Sidebar Click a guest row to open the Guest Reservations sidebar. The upper part of the sidebar shows the guest's name, phone number and tags, and below are the guest's reservations. Guest Reservations Guest Info Reservations in the sidebar are divided into groups: Upcoming — reservations in the Confirmed, Not Confirmed and Waitlist statuses; Current — reservations in the Started status; Past — reservations in the Ended and Cancelled statuses, no more than the last 10. To open a reservation, click it in the list. To open the Guest Info sidebar, click the block with the guest's name. It has two tabs: Profile — the guest's RFM segment, autotags and manual tags, loyalty number, loyalty bonuses, discount, sex and last visit. You can also add a manual tag to the guest here; Statistics — the guest's visit statistics. The button with the guest icon in the upper-right corner of the Guest Info sidebar opens the guest card in the main CosmosResto system.

title: Guest Profile
text: Open Guest Profile To open a guest profile: Go to Marketing → Guests Enter one of the following in the search bar: first name, last name, phone number, email address, or loyalty card number Click the required guest in the list to open their profile Guest Profile Guest Profile Tabs Guest Profile Tabs The guest profile consists of five tabs: ✔ Statistics ✔ Reservations ✔ Orders ✔ Activity Log ✔ Mailing Log Data Filtering Data Filtering To view statistics for a specific location or location group, select the required value from the location dropdown. To change the period used to calculate statistics, select the required period from the period dropdown. After changing the selected values, all metrics and charts on the page are recalculated automatically. Note. The Average Orders Per Month widget uses its own period selection and does not depend on the general page period. Personal Information Colon Button To edit the guest's personal information, click the button with the colon icon and select Edit. Make the required changes and click Save. For more information about changing a phone number, see Phone Numbers. Statistics When you open a guest profile, the Statistics tab is displayed by default. It contains information that helps you evaluate the guest's activity, visit history, and preferences. The data is presented as metrics and charts. Guest Profile Top 1\. Guest Avatar 2\. Note and Preferences 3\. Loyalty Program 4\. Average Check Per Order 5\. Average Party Size 6\. Avg Check Per Guest 7\. Average Orders Per Month 8\. Autotags and Manual Tags 9\. Visits 10\. Key Indicators Guest Profile Bottom 11\. Total Paid 12\. Top Categories 13\. Top Products 14\. Visit Time 1\. Guest Avatar RFM Hover over the guest avatar to view the guest's RFM information. The tooltip displays: ✔ current RFM Status ✔ RFM Score, if calculated ✔ a brief description of the current RFM Status For more information, see the RFM page. 2\. Note and Preferences Note The Note widget in the profile header contains two independent fields: ✔ Note — used to store general information about the guest and displayed only in the guest profile ✔ Preferences — used to store the guest's service preferences. They are displayed in the Waiter app and help employees take the guest's preferences into account Click the widget to view or edit both fields. 3\. Loyalty Program Loyalty Account The loyalty program widget is located at the top of the guest profile. It displays the balance of the bonus account linked to the loyalty card. Click the widget to open a list of all the guest's bonus accounts. The name and current balance are displayed for each account. If the guest does not participate in the loyalty program, the widget displays No Loyalty Card. 4\. Average Check Per Order Average Check Per Order Displays the average value of one guest order. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The chart shows how the average check changes as orders are placed. 5\. Average Party Size Average Party Size Displays the average number of guests per visit. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The chart shows how the average party size changes as orders are placed. 6\. Avg Check Per Guest Avg Check Per Guest Displays the average amount spent by one guest per visit. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The average check is calculated by dividing the total amount of the checks by the total number of guests specified in those checks. 7\. Average Orders Per Month Average Orders Per Month Displays the guest's average number of orders per month. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations. The widget uses its own period selection, independent of the general page period. The chart displays: a solid line — data for the selected period a dashed line — data for the previous equivalent period Note. Full calendar periods are used for the calculation. For example, Last Month means the last full calendar month, not the last 30 days. 8\. Tags Tags Widget The Tags widget displays Autotags and Manual Tags assigned to the guest. Hover over a tag to view its full name and description, if provided. To add Manual Tags, click the edit icon next to the Manual Tags field. In the window that opens, select the required tags. For more information, see the Manual Tags and Autotags pages. 9\. Visits Visits The widget displays information about the guest's visits. The data is calculated based on closed checks and cancelled reservations. The following information is displayed: ✔ total number of visits ✔ number of cancelled reservations ✔ date of the last visit ✔ percentage of visits and cancellations Note. The number of visits is calculated for all time and does not depend on the selected period. 10\. Key Indicators Key Indicators Displays the guest's key indicators for the selected period. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The following indicators are displayed: Total Paid Discount Checks Count Last Check Avg Check Avg Check Per Hour Avg Time Favorite Location The radial chart displays the relative values of the following indicators compared with other guests at the selected locations: ✔ Total Paid ✔ Discount ✔ Avg Check ✔ Avg Check Per Hour ✔ Avg Time When you hover over a point on the chart, the guest's position relative to other guests is displayed. For example: "The guest has higher Average Check than 39% of other guests." The value depends on the selected period and is recalculated when the period changes. For Avg Check Per Hour, only checks that meet at least one of the following conditions are included: ✔ check duration is at least 30 minutes ✔ check total is at least 50 AED for the UAE or 1,000 RUB for Russia 11\. Total Paid Total Paid Displays the guest's check totals in chronological order for the selected period. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The chart displays: X-axis — the sequence of checks Y-axis — the total amount of each check In Last 30 Checks mode, individual checks are displayed as points on the chart. Hover over a point to view: ✔ Location ✔ Check Date ✔ Visit Start and End Time ✔ Visit Duration ✔ Check Total Click a point to open the order details. 12\. Top Categories Top Categories Displays the three product categories with the highest total sales at the selected locations for the selected period. For each category, the following information is displayed: ✔ category name ✔ total sales ✔ number of items sold Note. Only categories with Guest Stats enabled in the Menu section are included in the calculation. For more details, see Menu. The chart displays: X-axis — the sequence of checks Y-axis — the category sales amount in each check 13\. Top Products Top Products Displays the five products with the highest total sales at the selected locations for the selected period. For each product, the following information is displayed: ✔ product name ✔ total sales ✔ number of items sold ✔ modifiers Hover over the modifiers to view a list of all modifiers and their quantities. 14\. Visit Time Visit Time Displays the start and end times of the guest's visits for the selected period. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The chart displays: X-axis — the sequence of checks Y-axis — time of day the start and end time of each visit visit duration as the area between the lines In Last 30 Checks mode, hover over a visit to view: ✔ location ✔ visit date ✔ start and end time ✔ visit duration ✔ check total Click a visit marker to open the order details. Blacklist Colon Button To add a guest to the blacklist, click the button with the colon icon and select Add to Blacklist. Blacklist When adding a guest to the blacklist, specify the reason and duration: Forever Until Date To remove a guest from the blacklist, click the button with the colon icon, select Remove from Blacklist, specify the reason, and confirm the action.

This allows users to access either the entire guest database or only the data for a selected Location Group. Example The Bakery group includes several bakeries in the chain. Employees of each bakery can work with the shared guest database of the Bakery group, regardless of which bakery in the group the guest previously visited. Location Groups can combine restaurants based on any criteria, such as region, brand, format, department, or other attributes. When creating a group, keep in mind that a user who has access to at least one location in the group automatically gets access to all locations included in that group. title: Kanban
text: Kanban is a reservation module mode in which the reservations of the selected day are arranged in status columns. It helps you see the flow of guests during the day and change a reservation status by dragging its card, without opening the sidebar. The mode opens from the left menu of the reservation module. The date is selected in the top panel and is shared by all modes: when you switch to Timeline or Floor Plan, the same day stays selected. Within a column, cards are sorted by reservation start time; in the Started and Ended columns - by end time. Kanban Reservation Card Clicking a card opens the reservation sidebar. For more information, read the article Editing and Canceling a Reservation. Reservation sidebar The card displays: guest phone number and name; guest card number; table number; start and end time; number of guests; comment icon, if there is a comment; how late the guest is, if the guest is late. Creating a Reservation The + button in the bottom right corner opens the creation of a new reservation. The button with a person icon above the + button creates a quick reservation for walk-in guests. Select the number of guests and click Create - the reservation immediately appears in the Started column, and a table is selected automatically. Changing the Status To change the status, drag the card to the required column. The status is saved immediately. If saving fails, an error message appears and the card returns to its place. Dragging a card It is not possible to drag: a cancelled reservation; a reservation that another employee is editing at the moment. Canceling a Reservation When you move a card to the Cancelled column, a cancellation form opens right in the column. Select a cancellation reason from the drop-down list and click Save. If you close the form without saving, the card returns to its original column. A cancelled reservation cannot be dragged to another column. Requests The Requests column displays new requests for the selected day and the following days, so the request card shows the visit date. A round icon on the right of the card means that the guest is already in the database. Clicking the icon opens the guest information: the guest's preferences, notes and tags help you choose a table. Requests column Requests cannot be dragged. Clicking a card expands it: it shows the request source and the buttons for processing the request: Confirm opens the reservation creation sidebar filled in with the request data; Reject opens a window for selecting the rejection reason. For more information about processing requests, read the article Processing Reservation Request. The board updates automatically: new requests, reservations and status changes made by other employees appear without reloading the page.
