title: Mailings
text: Mailings help maintain communication with guests: inform them about news and offers, bring guests back, remind them about the venue, and send service messages. Mailings The Mailings section is used to send messages to guests via SMS, Push, E-mail, and WhatsApp. Mailings There are two types of mailings: Auto — sent automatically when a specified event occurs. For example, when a guest enters a segment, registers in the loyalty program, or a check is closed Manual — launched by a user for a selected audience For each mailing, you can configure the audience, sending channel and message content, limits, sending time, and other parameters. The history and statuses of sent messages are available in the Mailing Log. Use the Auto / Manual switch to move between mailing types. Use the Active / Draft tabs to view active and saved mailings. To find a mailing, use the Search field. To create a new mailing, click Create. Instructions for creating mailings: Create Auto Mailing Create Manual Mailing Integrations Each sending channel in Mailings works through the corresponding integration: SMS — through an SMS gateway E-mail — through an E-mail service Push — through an integration with the loyalty card system WhatsApp — through an integration with Twilio If the required sending channel is not displayed when creating a mailing, check that the corresponding integration is available and configured. WhatsApp Templates Only templates approved by Meta can be used to send messages via WhatsApp. To create and manage templates, click Templates at the top of the Mailings page. For more information about working with templates, see Templates. Setting Limits To configure general limits on the number of messages sent to each guest, click the gear icon in the upper-right corner. Mailing Limits Limits are configured separately for each mailing type: Mass, Marketing, and Service For each type, limits can be configured separately for SMS, Push, E-mail, and WhatsApp A limit specifies the maximum number of messages that can be sent during the selected period If individual limits are configured for a specific mailing, the general limits are applied first, followed by the mailing's own limits Mailings with Extra Priority are sent without taking the general limits into account Sending Priority When creating a mailing, select High, Medium, or Low in the Priority field. The default value is Medium. The priority determines what share of sending a mailing gets when several mailings of the same channel are being sent at the same time. Messages are sent in batches: every 2 minutes, one batch is sent for each channel, and the batch size depends on the channel. In each batch, 70% of the places are reserved for high-priority mailings, 20% for medium-priority mailings, and 10% for low-priority mailings. That is why low-priority mailings do not wait for the others to finish - they are sent in parallel, just more slowly. If a priority level has fewer messages than its share, the free places go to messages with a higher priority. The priority works the same way for Auto and Manual mailings. For example, a large low-priority Manual Push mailing is being sent, and at the same time a high-priority Auto Push mailing is triggered. Messages of the Auto mailing take most of each batch and are sent faster, while the Manual mailing keeps being sent in parallel. Specifics: Priority is compared only between mailings of the same channel. For example, an SMS mailing does not affect the Push mailing queue. Priority does not affect limits. To send a mailing without taking the general limits into account, use Extra Priority. The priority of a started Manual mailing cannot be changed. If you change the priority of an Auto mailing, the new value applies only to new messages. Table Settings To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: Select the columns to display. Change the column order - drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name. Pin the required columns - click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table. Restore the default settings using Reset to Default. Mailings Mailings By default, the table displays the following columns: Name Description Status - the current status of the mailing. An Auto mailing can be Active or On pause, while a Manual mailing can be In progress, Finished or Stopped. Draft mailings do not have a status. Guest Amount - for Manual mailings only. The number of guests selected based on the mailing conditions at the time the mailing is launched. Channel - the channel used to send the message. Type - Mass, Marketing, or Service. Priority - High, Medium, or Low, see Sending Priority. Timezone - the timezone used by the mailing schedule. If an Auto mailing follows the timezone of the location where the event occurred, Trigger Event Timezone is displayed. Limits - for Auto mailings only. Individual mailing limits in the format N times per N days. If no limits are configured, a dash is displayed. Cost - the total cost of all messages sent by the mailing: for an Auto mailing, for the whole time it has been running; for a Manual mailing, the sum of all messages sent. The cost is calculated only for SMS; for other channels, a dash is displayed. The mailing cost is also shown on the mailing page next to its name. The following columns can also be enabled. When enabled, they are displayed in the table according to the column order in the settings: Author Created At Last Update Note. Table settings are saved after the page is refreshed. The settings are reset after you log out. Data Filtering Mailings If necessary, click Filters to set additional filtering conditions. After selecting the required values, click Apply. Applied filters are displayed above the table. To remove an individual filter, click × next to its name. To reset all filters, click Clear Filters.

title: Manual Tags
text: Manual tags allow users to manually label guests based on various characteristics. They are used to identify VIP guests, dietary restrictions, preferences, service requirements, and other information that should be taken into account when serving a guest. Unlike autotags, manual tags are assigned and removed by system users.

title: Marketing
description: Learn everything about the Marketing section: guest management, segmentation and tags, and ratings.

title: Master Chart
text: Master Chart allows you to analyze metrics for a selected period for one or several locations, compare data for different periods, and compare several metrics with each other. Data can be viewed in two modes: Chart — for analyzing metric trends Table — for viewing exact values by period. For more information, see Table Chart When switching between modes, the selected metrics and settings are kept. To get started, add at least one metric. For more information on creating and configuring metrics, see Create Metric. If there is no data for a metric with the selected settings, the metric remains in the legend but is not displayed on the chart. Master Chart Settings Settings 1\. Geo Defines the locations for which metrics are calculated. You can select one or several locations, a region, or World — all locations in all regions. How data for several selected locations is combined is set in the Location Mode setting. 2\. Period The period is calculated by cash shifts: the data includes shifts opened within the selected date range. 3\. Location Mode Defines how data for the selected locations is displayed: Total — data for the selected locations is combined. Several metrics can be displayed at the same time Separately — data for each location is displayed separately. Only one metric can be displayed at a time One VS Others — data for the selected location is compared with data for the other selected locations. Only one metric can be displayed at a time 4\. LFL LFL allows you to compare metrics for the selected period with another period using the same settings. Select the period for comparison: Previous Period — the previous period of the same length Same Period Last Year — the same period of the previous year Custom Period — a period set manually The change in percent is displayed for the compared values. 5\. Group By Data can be grouped by day, week, month, quarter, half-year, or year. The system automatically sets a suitable grouping depending on the selected period. If necessary, you can change it manually. Each point or bar on the chart corresponds to the selected grouping interval. For example, when grouping by week, metric values for each week are displayed. Chart Display Click the gear icon to change the chart display settings. Gear Show Lines — enables guide lines when hovering over the chart Show Values — displays values directly on the chart Show Filters — displays the filters applied to the metric in the tooltip on hover When hovering over a point or bar, information for the corresponding grouping interval is displayed: the period, the selected locations, and the metric name and value. If there are several metrics on the chart, the tooltip shows the value of each of them. Value Scales The chart can display two Y-axis scales at the same time: one on the left and one on the right. Scales are used for metrics with different units of measurement — for example, revenue and order count. Value scales If a metric requires a third scale to be displayed, the metric remains in the legend but is not displayed on the chart. Legend The legend shows all added metrics. The following actions are available for each metric: click the eye icon to hide or show the metric on the chart click the metric name to open its settings A hidden metric remains in the legend and is not removed from the Master Chart. If there is no data for a metric or it requires a third scale to be displayed, the metric remains in the legend but is not displayed on the chart. Table {#table} The Table mode shows the same data as the chart, but in table form. Use it when you need exact values for each period. The chart is better suited for analyzing trends. Table Table rows correspond to the selected grouping intervals, and the added metrics are displayed in separate columns. If there is no data for a certain period, the cell shows No Data. Location Mode affects the metric columns in the table: Total — one column per metric with the combined value for the selected locations Separately — a separate column per location for each metric One VS Others — two columns per metric: the selected location and the other locations combined When LFL is enabled, each metric shows the value for the selected period, the value for the comparison period, and the change in percent. Table Settings Click the settings icon next to the grouping selector. Table settings Cells Display Currency Convert 1 000 000 to M Display The Fractional Part Total Show Total Show Average Export Export is available in both Master Chart modes. The file is downloaded in CSV format. To export data, click the download icon in the upper-right corner of the chart or table. The export includes the displayed metrics, taking into account the selected period, grouping, and applied filters. Metrics hidden with the eye icon are not included in the export. In the Chart mode, detailed data is exported: metric values for each period for each selected location, and the totals for all locations. In the Table mode, the table is exported as it is displayed on the screen. The finished file is saved in the Export section at the bottom of the side menu and is available for download for 24 hours. Saving a Report Master Chart settings are kept during the current session. You can go to another section and return to the Master Chart without having to configure it again. To save a configured Master Chart for later use, click the save icon in the upper-right corner of the chart or table. The report saves the selected locations, period, metrics, and filters, as well as the current view mode — Chart or Table. Save Enter the report name and make it shared if necessary. By default, a report is private and available only to its author. A shared report is available to other users of the Analytics module. The list of saved reports is available on the Reports page.

title: Menu
text: The Cashbox → Menu section shows the menu of your locations: groups and products that CosmosResto receives from the POS system (iiko). Products cannot be created, renamed, or deleted in CosmosResto - all changes are made in the POS. The menu is synchronized with the POS once a day. New products, changes, and deactivated products appear in CosmosResto after the next synchronization. Menu Table The menu is displayed as a tree: groups expand and collapse, and contain nested groups and products. The nesting of groups is the same as in the POS menu. Menu Products and groups deactivated in the POS remain in the table and are shown with hatching. If a group is created in the POS but has no products yet, it is not displayed in CosmosResto. The group appears in the menu after at least one product is added to it and the next synchronization with the POS is completed. Search and Filters Search works across all menu levels: it finds not only top-level groups, but also nested groups and products at any depth. Search starts working after you enter 3 characters. Filters contain one filter - Status: Active or Deactivated. Guest Stats The guest profile has a Top Categories block - the three menu groups the guest has spent the most on. For more details, see Guest Profile. Top Categories By default, only top-level groups are counted. Everything the guest ordered within a group is added up into one amount. For example, beer, tea, and coffee from the Drinks group appear in the stats as one line - Drinks. If you want to see a nested group separately, for example how much the guest spends on beer, enable it for that group: right-click the group and select Add to Guest Stats. After that, beer is counted separately - Drinks / Beer, and Drinks includes everything else. To return the group to the total amount, select Remove from Guest Stats. Guest Stats The Guest Stats column shows whether a group is counted separately: a check mark means yes, a cross means no. Top-level groups, for example Drinks, are always counted separately - they always have a check mark, and it cannot be turned off. You can turn counting on and off only for nested groups. Products have a dash in this column: a single product is never shown in the stats separately, it is always included in the amount of its group. Product Photo A photo can be added only to a product - groups cannot have a photo. A product has one photo for all locations. The photo is kept after synchronization with the POS and after the product is deactivated. To add a photo, click the product - the Item Image page opens. If the product already has a photo, you can replace it, change its position, or delete it on this page. Item Image Photo requirements: JPG, JPEG, or PNG format; file size - up to 10 MB; width and height - up to 2000 px; recommended aspect ratio - 3:4. The photo is shown in the Waiter app: the waiter opens it by long-pressing the item in the menu and can show it to the guest. Waiter Export You can export the menu to a file using the export button in the upper right corner of the table. The file includes groups and products according to the Status filter: for example, if Active is selected, the file contains only active items. Without the filter, all items are exported, including deactivated ones. For each item, the group it belongs to is specified. Menu export
description: In this section, you will learn how the menu works in CosmosResto, how to count menu groups in guest stats, and how to add a product photo.

title: Multi-Table Reservation
text: Multi-table reservation is a reservation for 2 or more tables. This type of reservation has its own peculiarities and limitations, which we will discuss below. When creating a reservation for multiple tables, there should be no time gaps between all tables. The system will show itself if there is a time gap between tables in one reservation. Selecting Multiple Tables via Sidebar 1\. Open the table list. 2\. At the bottom enable the option Select multiple tables. 3\. You can also find a suitable table by name, filter tables by needed criteria and sort the list. 4\. Select the required tables, then click Apply. Selecting Multiple Tables via Timeline 1\. Open the section Timeline. 2\. By holding and dragging to the side, select the tables you are interested in. 3\. In the opened sidebar, fill in the remaining reservation data. All fields for creating a reservation are described in more detail in this article.
description: Reservation for multiple tables

title: Online Reservation Schedule
text: The online reservation schedule defines on which days of the week and at what hours guests can make a reservation online. The schedule is set separately for each location. To open the schedule, go to Reservations → Settings, select the location in the Location field and open the tab with the clock icon in the upper right corner. Viewing the Schedule The tab shows the Online Reservation Schedule block - cards for all days of the week. The card of an open day shows the start and end time of the interval and its Duration. A closed day shows Closed. Online reservation schedule Editing the Schedule After clicking Edit in the upper right corner, the schedule opens for editing: Editing the schedule Online Reservation available - the general online reservation switch for the location. If it is turned off, online reservations are unavailable at the location and the schedule by day is hidden. Open - the switch for each day. If it is off, the day is closed for online reservations and its time fields are not shown. Opens At and Closes At - the start and end of the interval when online reservations are available. Both fields are required for an open day. The interval duration is shown below the fields. To apply the changes, click Save. Schedule in the Widget The schedule applies to all reservation widgets of the location. In the widget form, the guest can choose a visit start time only within the interval of the selected day. Time in the reservation widget A closed day has no interval, so the widget does not offer any time for that day. If all days are closed, online reservations are unavailable. The latest available start time is the closing time minus the visit duration. For example, with an interval of 10:00 - 22:00 and a 1-hour visit, the latest time is 21:00.
description: In this section you will learn how to set the days and time intervals available to guests for online reservations at a location.

title: Orders
text: The Orders tab contains a list of all orders associated with the selected guest. Orders Page View an Order Click a row in the table. A window with the order details will open, where you can view the items included in the order. Order Details Order Changelog To see what actions were performed with the order on the POS terminal, click Open Changelog in the Order Details window. Changelog button The Changelog window will open. Each action with the order is shown as a separate row in the table: Log Type - for example, adding or removing an item, changing the quantity, sending an item to the kitchen, printing a precheck, closing the order Log Details - the item and its quantity, the amount, or other data of the action Occurred At - the date and time in the location's time zone Updated By - the employee who performed the action. If the author is unknown, a dash is displayed By default, the newest events are shown at the top. To change the order, click the Occurred At column name. Changelog To display only the events you need, click Filters and select values in the Log Type and Updated By filters. Changelog filters The changelog is based on data sent by the plugin on the POS terminal. For orders opened before the changelog was introduced, it may be missing or incomplete. Summary Click Summary at the bottom of the window. Summary information about the total amount of orders matching the selected filters will be displayed. Order Total Note. The calculation includes all orders matching the selected filters. Orders Table The table displays information about the selected guest's orders. To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ select the columns to display ✔ change the column order — drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name ✔ pin the required columns — click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table ✔ restore the default settings using Reset to Default Column Wizard By default, the following columns are displayed in the table: Status — the current order status: Open, Closed, or Returned Cash Shift — the date of the cash shift in which the order was closed Location Order Start Time End Time Duration — the time between opening and closing the order. It is not calculated for open orders Served By — the employee who served the table, including their role and grade Price — the order amount before discounts Discount Discount % Total — the final amount to be paid You can also enable the following columns. Their position in the table follows the column order in the table settings: Reservation — the reservation number associated with the order Table — the table number specified in the order Party Size — the number of guests specified in the order Cashier — the employee who closed the order, including their role and grade Note. Table settings are saved after the page is refreshed and when switching between guest profiles. The settings are reset after you log out. Data Filtering Orders Filter Select the required location from the list to display only orders associated with that location. To change the displayed period, select the required date range. If necessary, click Filters to set additional filtering conditions. After selecting the required values, click Apply. Applied filters are displayed above the table. To remove an individual filter, click × next to its name. To reset all filters, click Clear Filters. Note. Selected filters are saved after the page is refreshed and when switching between guest profiles. The filters are reset after you log out.

title: POS Integration
text: The Settings → POS Integration section links CosmosResto payment types to the payment types of the POS system (iiko). Mapping is required so that payments for orders from the POS are correctly recorded in CosmosResto. CosmosResto has three payment types: Cash, Card and Bonuses. iiko usually has more payment types, so several iiko payment types can be mapped to one CosmosResto payment type. Payment Types Table Mapping is set up separately for each location. The location is selected in the Location field above the table. POS Integration The table contains the following columns: Payment Type Name - the CosmosResto payment type. The list is fixed: payment types cannot be added or removed. POS Reference - the iiko payment types mapped to the CosmosResto payment type. If several types are mapped, the first one is shown with a counter of the rest (for example, +1). If there is no mapping, a dash is shown. Sync Status - the mapping state: Synced - the payment type is mapped to iiko, Not Synced - the payment type has not been mapped yet. Payment Type Mapping Mapping is set up in the Edit Mapping window, which opens when you click a table row. The window shows the CosmosResto payment type and the location for which the mapping is being set up. In the POS References field, select one or more iiko payment types. The list offers Search and Select All. Confirm the selection with Apply and save the mapping with Save. Selected types are shown in the field, and an unneeded one can be removed with the cross. Edit Mapping iiko payment types list One iiko payment type can be mapped to only one CosmosResto payment type. Changing the mapping may significantly affect how the POS system works. Before saving, make sure the selected iiko payment types belong to the correct CosmosResto payment type. Refreshing Data The list of payment types is loaded from iiko. The Refresh Data button in the upper right corner of the page starts synchronization with the POS: it loads new payment types and updates existing ones. Use it after a payment type has been added or renamed in iiko. If the POS References field shows Nothing here yet, the data from iiko has not been loaded yet. Click Refresh Data. If the list is still empty, check the iiko connection or contact CosmosResto support.
description: In this section, you will learn how to map CosmosResto payment types to the payment types of the iiko POS system and how to refresh data from the POS.

title: Processing Reservation Request
text: Basic information about the request entity is described in this article. Here we describe how to process requests and all possible interactions with them. How to Process a Request Three main actions are available for an active request: Reject; Make a reservation; Open guest profile, if found in the system. Converting a Request to a Reservation Open the request. Click Confirm. If the guest was not previously in the system, fill in and confirm the new guest data. Check the visit date and time, specify the duration. Check the number of guests. Select one or more tables. Check the comment. Check or create guest profile. Save the reservation. After saving, the request receives the status Converted to reservation. The new reservation appears on the timeline, floor plan and reservations table according to standard rules. Before saving, check the availability of the selected time and tables. When submitting a request, the guest can select any 15-minute interval available in the widget without taking into account the current occupancy of the establishment. The set of available intervals is determined by the location's operating hours. The reservation source is transferred from the request. It cannot be changed either when creating the reservation or when editing it later. Rejecting a Request Reject the request if the establishment cannot accept the request or the guest declined the visit. Open the request. Click Reject. Select a reason. Confirm the action. Available reasons: No available seats; Cancelled by guest; Undesirable guest; Error; Technical reasons. After rejection, the request receives the status Rejected. It is no longer displayed among active requests on the timeline and floor plan. In the table, the record is retained for viewing, but actions with it become unavailable. Opening Guest Profile The button to go to the profile is available if the system found the guest by phone number and linked them to the request. Open the request. Click on the guest's name or the profile transition button. View or supplement the guest data. If the profile is not found, the request displays the data entered in the form. Guest Tags from Widget If manual guest tag selection is configured in the widget, their application depends on whether the profile is found. If the guest is found, selected tags are applied to their profile. If the guest is not found, tags are saved inside the request. Deferred tags are applied after creating the guest profile when converting the request to a reservation. Before creating a profile, tags from the request are not applied to the guest. Notifications If corresponding templates are configured in reservation settings, the system can send messages to guests for events: Request creation; Request rejection. Read further: — Reservation Requests
description: Description of reservation request processing functionality via external services

title: Publishing and Distributing a Survey
text: After creation, a survey is saved as a draft. For respondents to be able to complete it, the survey must be published. After the first publication, the system creates a permanent public link and makes the survey available for connecting to mailings. Publishing a Survey A survey with the status Draft or Unpublished can be published. Open the survey. Check its structure and settings. Specify the survey completion period (applies to personal links, more on this below) Click Publish. Confirm publication in the modal window. When publishing, the system saves the current changes and validates the form. Upon successful publication: The status changes to Published; A public link is created upon first publication; The survey becomes available for selection in mailings. Upon republishing, a new public link is not created. The system reactivates the link generated at the first publication. Public Link The public link is intended for open completion of the survey without being tied to a specific guest. Features: Suitable for a QR code, website, social networks and other open channels; Responses can be sent via one public link with no limit on the number of completions; If the survey is unpublished or deactivated, the public link becomes unavailable for completion and copying. Personal Link A personal link is generated for a specific guest when the survey is sent via a mailing. Through it, the system can link the received response to the guest's profile. Features: A response can be submitted via one link only once; The link has a limited validity period. Survey Completion Period The Survey completion period parameter determines how long the personal link remains valid from the moment the message is sent. The default is 3 days. If you change the completion period, the new value applies to all personal links for this survey, including those already sent. After the period expires, the respondent will see a message that the survey is unavailable. Sending a Survey via Mailing To add a survey to a mailing message: Open the creation or editing of a mailing in the Marketing -> Mailings section. At the Content step, add the Survey link variable to the message text. In the Related survey field, select the required survey. Save the mailing settings. The Related survey field is required. The list displays only published surveys. When sending, the system generates a personal link for each recipient. Additionally, the system checks: The guest must not be unsubscribed from survey mailings; For an automatic mailing with the Closed check trigger, the survey's location must match the order's location. In the current implementation, the response location is determined automatically only for responses received from an automatic mailing with the Closed check trigger. For other methods of receiving a response, the location field may be empty. Related Mailings The Distribution tab displays a block of related mailings. For each mailing, its name and current status are shown. This allows you to see where the current survey is being used. Unpublishing a Survey A survey with the status Published can be unpublished. Open the published survey. Click Unpublish. Confirm the action. After confirmation: The status changes to Unpublished; The public link stops working; The survey becomes unavailable for new connections in mailings; Active mailings using this survey are switched to the status Paused. Unpublishing does not save the current unsaved changes to the form. Save your changes before performing this action. Republishing An unpublished survey can be published again. Republishing follows the same steps as the initial publication. In this case, the previous public link is used. Related mailings previously switched to the status Paused are not automatically resumed. They must be activated separately.
description: Publishing a survey, public and personal links, mailings, unpublishing and deactivation.

title: Reports
text: The Reports page shows saved Master Chart reports. Reports Reports are divided into two tabs: Shared — reports available to other users of the Analytics module Private — personal reports available only to their author To find a report, use the search by name. Report Actions Click the two-dot button on the report card to open the actions menu: Report actions Edit Duplicate Copy Link Delete Duplicating a report opens the window for saving a new report. If the original report is available to other users, its copy can be saved as a private report and changed independently of the original. Filters If necessary, click Filters to set additional filtering conditions. Filters After selecting the required values, click Apply. Applied filters are displayed above the list of reports. To remove a single filter, click × next to its name. To reset all filters, click Clear Filters.

title: Requests
text: To open requests, tap Menu at the top of the screen and select requests. A request card shows the guest's phone number and name, the date and time for which the guest wants to book a table, and the number of guests. The time next to the clock shows how long the request has been waiting, for example 0m. If the guest is already in the database, the request card has a button with a guest icon. It opens the guest info - see the Reservation View article. To process a request, tap it. The card expands and shows the request Source, the guest's comment and the Reject and Confirm buttons. Requests Confirming a Request Tap Confirm. If the guest is not in the database yet, the Add New Guest window opens: the first name, last name and phone number are taken from the request. Select Male or Female and tap Add Guest. Adding a Guest If the guest is already in the database, this step is skipped. Then the reservation form opens, filled in with the request data: guest, date, time, number of guests and source. If the guest is already in the database, the guest's tags are shown under the name. Select a table, change other fields if needed and tap Create. The Send SMS switch at the bottom of the form is on by default. Rejecting a Request Tap Reject. In the Reject Request window, select the Rejection reason - the field is required. For the guest to receive an SMS about the rejection, turn on Send SMS; the switch is off by default. Tap Reject. A rejected request cannot be restored. Rejecting a Request
description: How to work with reservation requests in the CosmosResto Reservations app on the phone.

title: Reservation List
text: The Reservations → Reservation List section shows reservations of the selected locations for the selected period as a table. Here you can find a reservation, filter the list, configure the displayed columns and export data. This is a section of the main CosmosResto system. The table view inside the reservation module is described in the article Reservation Timeline. Reservation List Page Elements Page Elements Geo — selection of locations whose reservations are displayed in the table. Period — the date and time range for which reservations are displayed. Switch — the left button opens the reservation list, the right one opens the request list. For more information about requests, read the article Reservation Requests. Reservation Statistics Reservation statistics for the selected period are displayed in the lower-right corner of the table. They have two tabs: Active and Cancelled. Statistics: active Statistics: cancelled On the Active tab, the total number and the number in each status are displayed for guests and reservations: Waitlist, Not Confirmed, Confirmed, Started, Ended. On the Cancelled tab, the data is grouped by cancellation reason. Only the reasons that have cancelled reservations are displayed. The Summary column shows the total number of cancelled reservations. The Guests row shows the number of guests in the reservations, while the Reservations row shows the number of reservations. Reservation Details Click a row in the table to open the sidebar with the reservation details: guest, table, start and end time, party size, the employee assigned to the reservation, and status. The Changelogs button opens the list of all changes to this reservation. The Linked Orders block shows the numbers of the orders linked to the reservation. Reservation Details Click an order number to open the Order Details window over the sidebar. The window shows the order data, the order items, and the totals. Order Details Table Settings To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ Select the columns to display ✔ Change the column order — drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name ✔ Pin the required columns — click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table ✔ Restore the default settings using Reset to Default Table Settings By default, the table displays the following columns: Guest Phone Tags — guest tags Loyalty Card Order — the number of the order opened at the reservation table Status Tables Party Size Duration Start Time End Time Deposit — the deposit amount for the reservation Reservation Tags — tags assigned to the reservation. For more information, read the article Reservation Tags Reservation Notes Reservation Location — the location where the reservation was created Served By — the employee assigned to the reservation The following columns can be enabled additionally. When enabled, they appear in the table according to the column order in the settings: Guest Notes Reservation — the reservation number Cancellation Reason — filled in only for cancelled reservations Total — the total amount of the orders linked to the reservation Reservation Source Updated At Updated By Created At Created By Filters Click Filters, select a field in the list on the left and check the required values on the right. To apply the conditions, click Apply. Filters Applied filters are displayed next to the Filters button. To remove a filter, click × next to its name. Export To export reservations, click the download icon in the upper-right corner of the table, next to the table settings button. After that, the system creates an export task. When the file is ready, the Export Successful notification with the Download button appears. The file is also available in the Export section at the bottom of the side menu. The file can be downloaded within 24 hours. The file includes all reservations that match the selected geo, period and filters, from all pages of the table. Only the columns enabled in the table settings are exported. The file is exported in CSV format. Export is available only in the reservation list. There is no export button in the request list. Export
description: In this section you will learn how to work with the reservation list: search and filter reservations, configure the table and export data.

title: Reservation List
text: CosmosResto Reservations on the phone is an app for working with reservations without a computer or tablet. Installation and login are described in the Reservations article. After login, the list of reservations for the current date opens. Reservations are grouped by status in the following order: Not Confirmed, Confirmed, Started, Ended, Cancelled. The number of reservations in a group is shown next to its name. Reservation List Reservation Card Reservation Cards A reservation card shows: the guest's phone number and name, loyalty card number; the table - if the reservation is for several tables, the number of the other tables is shown next to it, for example +1. A lock next to the table means that Don't Change is on in the reservation: the table and the guest cannot be changed; start and end time, number of guests; a comment icon if the reservation has a comment; the table's minimum spend - how much has already been spent out of the amount that has to be spent at this table, for example 3K/26K DH; the time until the guest arrives. If another employee is editing the reservation at the moment, the card shows the name of this employee. To open a reservation, tap its card - see the Reservation View article. Screen Elements Screen Elements Menu - opens and closes the menu of the app sections. The open section is highlighted with a frame. Floor Plan Reservation List Requests Profile - see below. \+ - creating a reservation, see the Creating a Reservation article. Profile The profile opens from the menu. Here you can turn Web Push notifications on or off and select the Language and the Location you work with. Lock Screen locks the app, Log Out logs you out of the account. Profile
description: The main screen of the CosmosResto Reservations app on the phone - the list of reservations for the selected date.

title: Reservation Module
description: In this section you will learn everything about reservations. How to create and edit reservations, as well as how to navigate in the section.

title: Reservation Requests
text: Reservation requests help you process guest requests sent through a website widget or supported external reservation service. A request captures the desired date, time and visit parameters, but does not automatically reserve a table. For the request to become a reservation, an employee must check the data and confirm it manually. You can work with requests in all views of the reservation module: on the timeline, floor plan and a separate requests table. Brief Work Scenario Guest submits a form in the widget on the website or external reservation service. The request appears in the reservation module. An employee opens the request, checks the data and contacts the guest if necessary. The request can be: Accepted and converted to a reservation Rejected After confirmation, the table is reserved with a standard reservation. A request and a reservation are different entities. Until the request is converted to a reservation, the selected time is not considered occupied and the table is not reserved. How a request is created: A request is created manually by a guest through a reservations widget. The system links the request to an existing profile if the guest is found. Saves the data inside the request if the guest is not found. Passes the request to the reservation module for manual processing by an employee. A new guest profile is not created automatically at this stage. Displaying and Working with Requests You can work with requests in all views of the reservation module. When a new request arrives, the counter of the Requests button increases. It shows the number of requests with New status or requests being processed. Requests in Table Requests Go to the reservation module. Go to the Requests tab. Click on the row to open the request sidebar. The table columns are described in the Table Settings section. Search, filtering and sorting: In the table you can search requests by first name, last name and phone number. Filtering is available by visit date, guest, request status, source and comment text. The source filter shows only the sources connected in the venue. By default, requests are sorted: By date and time of desired visit — from closest to later ones. By processing wait time — first requests that have been in New status longer. Requests with Rejected status are not displayed unless explicitly specified in the filter. This sorting helps you process the closest and longest-waiting requests first (it is important to set the current status first). In the requests table you can also create a reservation by clicking the + button in the lower right part of the section. Statistics: Request statistics are displayed in the lower-right corner of the table. They have two tabs: Requests — the total number of requests and the number of new and converted requests; Rejected — the total number of rejected requests (the Summary column) and the number for each rejection reason. Only the reasons that have rejected requests are displayed. Table Settings {#table-settings} To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ Select the columns to display ✔ Change the column order — drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name ✔ Pin the required columns — click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table ✔ Restore the default settings using Reset to Default Table settings By default, the table displays the following columns: Guest — the guest's name from the profile if the guest is found in the system, or the name entered in the form Phone Date of Birth Start Time — the desired date and time the visit starts End Time — the desired date and time the visit ends Party Size Time in Request — how long the request has been in New status Request Source — the channel the request came from. Filled in automatically Email Telegram Tags — tags selected by the guest in the widget Status The following columns can be enabled additionally. When enabled, they appear in the table according to the column order in the settings: Note Rejection reason — filled in only for rejected requests Requests on Timeline Go to the reservation module. Open the Timeline view. Click Requests. In the opened sidebar, select the required card. Requests on Floor Plan Go to the reservation module. Open the Floor Plan view. In the sidebar switch from the Reservations tab to Requests. Select a request. A request is not displayed on the floor plan as an occupied table. The table will be marked as occupied only after the request is converted to a reservation. Unlike other views, a system guest is immediately available here if linked to the request. Other data is pulled from the request. Request Card The request card displays: Guest name specified in the form; Phone number; Desired visit date and time; Number of guests; Comment; Source; Time elapsed since the request was created. After opening the card, processing actions become available. Original request data cannot be changed, but a reservation can be created based on them. Request Statuses A request can have the following statuses: New — request has entered the system, but the employee has not yet taken action. Rejected — employee declined the request. Converted to reservation — a reservation has been created based on the request. Processing mark — the request is currently being opened or edited by an employee (status is indicated by an edit icon). Rejected and Converted to reservation statuses are final. After transitioning to one of them, the request is no longer considered active. Enabling New Request Notifications In the reservation module, click on your avatar to open the action menu. Select Enable notifications. Allow Show notifications in the popup window in the browser. Check that notifications are enabled in your browser's system settings. Read further: — Processing Reservation Request
description: Description of reservation request functionality via external services

title: Reservation Sources
text: Depending on how a venue works, it uses different reservation sources and cancellation reasons. Three lists are set up for each location: Reservation Sources - available when creating and editing a reservation. Reservation Cancellation Reason - available when cancelling a reservation, including a reservation on the waitlist. Request Rejection Reason - available when rejecting a request. In each list you choose the values available to staff and one default value. The default value is filled in automatically when a staff member creates a reservation, cancels it or rejects a request. To open the settings, go to Reservations → Settings, select the location in the Location field and open the fourth tab in the upper right corner. Reservation sources and cancellation reasons To change the lists, click Edit - a pencil icon appears next to the name of each block. It opens a window with all possible values: check the ones you need or click Select All, then click Apply. The default value cannot be unchecked in this window - first choose another default value. To apply the changes, click Save. Reservation Sources By default, the sources Phone Call, Walk-in, Messenger and Website are available at a location. The other standard sources - Email, Social Media, Staff, Partner, Concierge Service, Event Agency - can be enabled in the selection window opened by the pencil icon. Selecting reservation sources Default Source - the source that is automatically filled in when a reservation is created manually. In the reservation it can be changed to another source from the list. The source of a reservation from the widget or from Yandex is set automatically and does not depend on this setting. In a reservation created from a request, the source is taken from the request and cannot be changed. Custom Reservation Sources In addition to the standard sources, you can add your own source, for example the name of a concierge service or a partner. To do this, click Add source, enter a name and save. Add source A custom source has a three-dot icon instead of a cross. It opens a menu: Remove from list - makes the source unavailable for selection, like the cross on standard sources. The source is not deleted: to bring it back, open the selection window with the pencil icon and check the source again. Rename. Deactivate - disables the source permanently. Reservations with this source are kept, but the source cannot be restored after deactivation. Custom source menu Reservation Cancellation Reason Cancellation reasons are available when cancelling a reservation, including a reservation on the waitlist. The value of the Default Reason field is filled in automatically and can be changed to another reason from the list. Possible reasons are divided into groups: Guest-related: Guest Cancellation, No Confirmation, Impossible Changes, Deposit Disagreement, Late Arrival, Guest Didn't Show, Invalid Data. Venue-related: No Available Seats, Venue Closed, Technical Issues, Guest Non-Compliance, Guest Unwanted. Operational: Merge With Another Booking, Transfer to Another Location, Rescheduled. Administrative: Mistake, Duplicate. Reasons are chosen in the window opened by the pencil icon next to the Reservation Cancellation Reason block. Pencil next to cancellation reasons In the window, check the reasons you need. The reasons already selected are shown on the right. Selecting reservation cancellation reasons Request Rejection Reason Rejection reasons are available when rejecting a request. They are chosen from the same groups as cancellation reasons, but are set up separately, with their own value in the Default Reason field. Reasons are chosen in the window opened by the pencil icon next to the Request Rejection Reason block. Pencil next to rejection reasons In the window, check the reasons you need. The reasons already selected are shown on the right. Selecting request rejection reasons Values Removed From the List If a value is removed from the list or deactivated, saved reservations do not change: In reservations where it was selected, the value is still displayed. Statistics for this value are kept. Such a value cannot be selected in a new or existing reservation. If it is replaced with another value in a reservation and the changes are saved, the previous value cannot be returned. The filters of the reservation and request lists offer only the values enabled in the settings.
description: In this section you will learn how to choose the reservation sources, reservation cancellation reasons and request rejection reasons available at a location.

title: Reservation Statuses
text: Status shows the current state of a reservation: whether it is confirmed, if the guest is in the establishment or the reservation was cancelled. You can specify the status in the sidebar when creating or editing a reservation. Five reservation statuses are provided: Not confirmed Confirmed In progress Completed Cancelled Statuses Cancelled and Completed are only available when editing a reservation. INDICATORS AND ALERTS The color of the reservation card helps quickly determine its current status. Color Indicators on Timeline: Yellow — status "Confirmed" Orange — status "Not confirmed" Green — status "In progress" Dark green — status "Completed" Pink — status "Not confirmed", if guest is late Light blue — status "Confirmed", if guest is late Red — status "Cancelled" Color Indicators on Floor Plan: Yellow — status "Confirmed" Orange — status "Not confirmed" Green — status "In progress" Pink — status "Not confirmed", if guest is late Light blue — status "Confirmed", if guest is late Additional Alerts: Text alerts for late arrival — displayed on the reservation card on the timeline from the first minute of guest delay. Text alerts for reservation end — shows how much time remains until the end of the guest's visit. Read further: — Creating a Reservation
description: Description of reservation statuses

title: Reservation Tags
text: Reservation tags help you manually mark reservations within the CRM. With their help you can visually highlight important records, quickly understand the context of a reservation, group reservations and find them using filters. For example, you can create tags Needs parking, Late arrival, High priority or Requires manager attention. Reservation tags are not related to guest tags. These are separate types of tags that are configured and used independently of each other. Tag List In the section Reservations -> Reservation Tags a list of created tags and basic information about them is displayed. In this section you can view, create and edit tags. Search, filtering and sorting Search: by Name field — search begins after entering at least three characters. Filtering: by Locations, Creation/Update Date, Author. Sorting: by name, short name, creation date or last update date. Creating a Tag 1\. Open the section Reservations -> Reservation Tags. 2\. Click Create. 3\. Fill in the fields: Locations — when adding a tag to a reservation, the system shows only tags available for the selected location Name Short name — abbreviation that is displayed on the reservation Tooltip text — displayed when hovering over the tag Description Color Icon 4\. If necessary, add a description, icon and tooltip text. 5\. Click Save. After saving, the tag will appear in the general tag list and will be available in the tag list when editing a reservation. Editing a Tag In an existing tag you can edit all fields. After saving changes apply to all reservations that use the tag. Before saving, the system warns that the change may affect related reservations. Details of tag changes and creation can be seen inside the tag card. Deleting a Tag Open the section Reservations -> Reservation Tags. Find the required tag. Click on the tag, opening editing. Click Delete. Confirm deletion. After deletion: The tag will completely disappear from the system; The tag will be removed from all associated reservations; The tag will become unavailable for assignment and filtering; The change log of reservations where this tag was previously specified will not change. Using Tags in Reservations Adding a Tag Multiple tags can be assigned to one reservation. Only tags available for the location of this reservation are displayed in the list. Open the required reservation. Click Add tag. Find the tag by name or select it from the list. If necessary, select other tags. Click Save. After saving, the selected tags will be associated with the reservation and appear in its side panel. Removing a Tag from a Reservation Open the reservation. Click the delete icon next to the tag. Click Save. The tag will be removed only from the selected reservation. The tag itself will remain available in the system and will continue to be used in other reservations. Change History The system saves actions with tags in the reservation history. The time and author of tag addition or removal can be seen in the Change Log. Filtering Reservations by Tags Open the section Reservations. Go to table display mode. Open the filter by tags. Select one or more tags. The table will show only reservations matching the selected conditions. Tags of the selected location are available for filtering.
description: In this section you will learn everything about reservation tags. Creation, editing, application.

title: Reservation Timeline
text: The module has three display modes for reservations. Each one is suitable for different tasks: working with reservations, analyzing occupancy and managing guest seating. Timeline Floor Plan Table Timeline Timeline is an area with a time scale on which all reservations are displayed. Timeline Main elements: List of floors and tables. Floors can be collapsed and expanded. Time scale with reservations. Button to create a reservation. Statistics of completed reservations for the day. Information on reservations on the selected floor. Colors correspond to the status model. No Table, Requests and Waitlist buttons — open the corresponding lists in the sidebar on the right. Archive button — opens the list of canceled reservations. No Table, Requests and Waitlist The counter on each button shows the number of records in the corresponding list. No Table — reservations that have not yet been assigned a table. Requests — reservation requests received through the website widget. Click a request to view detailed information. A request can be rejected or confirmed and used to create a reservation. When creating a reservation, you can select a table, leave the reservation without a table or set the Waitlist status. For more information about working with requests, read the article Reservation Requests. Waitlist — records for which a reservation cannot be confirmed yet, for example if there is no suitable table or the required time is unavailable. A record does not reserve a table and does not block time. When it becomes possible to confirm the reservation, the record can be converted into a regular reservation. For more information about working with the waitlist, read the article Waitlist. Creating a Reservation on Timeline You can create a reservation directly on the timeline in several ways: Single click opens a sidebar to create a reservation. Click and drag right or left allow you to immediately set the reservation duration. Drag up or down allows you to select multiple tables at once (more about multi-reservation). You can also create a reservation via the Reservation creation button in the lower right corner. More about ways to create a reservation — in the article Creating a Reservation. Table List When you select a table, information about it is displayed: Layout and maximum capacity. Tags. Deposits and exclusions. In this same window you can add a block on a table for the selected period. The block is displayed on the timeline and floor plan, but does not prevent creating a reservation on this table. To block a table you need to specify: One or more tables. Block start time and duration. Reason for blocking. Floor Plan Floor plan is a visual representation of the establishment's tables, which allows you to assess the hall occupancy and manage reservations tied to specific tables. More about the floor plan in the article Floor Plan. Table Display of Reservations In this mode, reservations are displayed as a table. Records can be sorted and filtered. Also, a summary of reservations is displayed in the section taking into account the applied filters. Page elements: Button to refresh table data. Setting of displayed columns. Summary of reservations based on selected filters. Data in the table does not update automatically. If the data has changed, the update button will notify you. To load current information, click Refresh. Read further: — Floor Plan — Creating a Reservation
description: Navigation and functionality of the Timeline

title: Reservation View
text: To open a reservation, tap its card in the reservation list. Opening a Reservation The reservation opens with all its details: guest, table, date, time and duration, number of guests, source, comment and status. The guest's tags are shown under the guest's name. You can change the details and tap Save. Reservation Guest Info To see the guest info, tap the guest in the reservation. The info is split into two tabs: Profile and Statistics. The Profile tab shows: the guest's name and phone number; Autotags and Manual Tags - a manual tag can be added with Add Tag or removed with the cross; Loyalty Number, Loyalty Bonuses, Discount; Sex and Last Visit; the guest's note. Guest Profile The Statistics tab shows: Visits - how many times the guest came, cancelled a reservation or did not show up, in percent and in numbers; Last Check - the button opens the guest's last order; Top Products - what the guest orders most often, with Top Modifiers for them. Guest Statistics To replace the guest in the reservation, tap Change Guest at the bottom of the screen.

text: A reservation widget is a form on the venue website where guests submit reservation requests themselves. Requests from the widget arrive in the system; how to process them is described in Reservation Requests.

title: Reservations
text: The Reservations tab contains a list of all reservations associated with the selected guest. Here you can view the reservation history, including active, completed, and cancelled reservations. Reservation List Reservation View Click a row in the table to open the sidebar with the reservation details. The Linked Orders block shows the numbers of the orders linked to the reservation. Click an order number to open the Order Details window. Reservation View Reservation Summary Click Summary at the bottom of the window. Reservation Summary Cancelled Reservations Summary Use the Active / Cancelled switch to view a summary of active and cancelled reservations. For active reservations, the data is grouped by status; for cancelled reservations, by cancellation reason. Only the reasons that have cancelled reservations are displayed. The Guests row shows the number of guests in the reservations, while the Reservations row shows the number of reservations. Note. The summary is calculated based on all reservations matching the selected filters. Table Management The table displays information about the selected guest's reservations. To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ select the columns to display ✔ change the column order — drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name ✔ pin the required columns — click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table ✔ restore the default settings using Reset to Default Column Selection By default, the following columns are displayed in the table: Status — the current reservation status: Not Confirmed, Confirmed, Started, Ended, or Cancelled Location Start Time End Time Duration Deposit — the deposit progress Tables Party Size You can also enable the following columns. Their position in the table follows the column order in the table settings: Reservation — the unique reservation number Cancellation Reason Reservation Note Reservation Source — the source specified when the reservation was created Order — the order number associated with the reservation. If multiple orders are associated with the reservation, multiple order numbers are displayed Created At Created By — the employee who created the reservation, including their role and grade Note. Table settings are saved after the page is refreshed and when switching between guest profiles. The settings are reset after you log out. Data Filtering Reservations with Filters Select the required location from the list to display only reservations associated with that location. To change the displayed period, select the required date range. If necessary, click Filters to set additional filtering conditions. After selecting the required values, click Apply. Applied filters are displayed above the table. To remove an individual filter, click × next to its name. To reset all filters, click Clear Filters. Note. Selected filter values are saved after the page is refreshed and when switching between guest profiles. The filters are reset after you log out.

title: Responses and Working with Responses
text: The Responses section is used for viewing and analyzing survey results. Responses can be opened within a specific survey or in the general table across all available surveys. Within a survey, only responses for that survey are displayed. The general Responses table displays responses for all surveys available to you. responses Table Settings To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ Select the columns to display ✔ Change the column order — drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name ✔ Pin the required columns — click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table ✔ Restore the default settings using Reset to Default Table Settings By default, the table displays the following columns: Response At — date and time the response was submitted by the respondent. Survey Name Location — the location associated with the response. Automatically determined for responses from an automatic mailing based on the Closed check trigger; in other cases it may be absent. Response Source — shows how the response entered the system: Mailing, Public link or Entered manually. Added By — for a manual response, shows the employee who entered the data. Guest Phone Text Responses — the number of text comments in the response, including text in the Custom option field. Ratings — ratings left in Rating (marked with a star) and NPS (marked with a smiley) type questions. The icon color depends on the rating value on the question's scale. The following columns can be enabled additionally. When enabled, they appear in the table according to the column order in the settings: Response Channel — delivery channel, if the survey was sent via mailing. For a public link and manual entry, the field may be empty. Trigger — the event after which the mailing was sent. Triggered At — date and time of the event. Tables — tables associated with the event. Served By — employees who served the guest. E-mail Sex Birthday Favorite Location Last Visit Total Paid Checks Last Check Avg Check Avg Check Per Hour Loyalty Number Loyalty Discount Loyalty Registration Device — Mobile or Desktop, depending on the device from which the response was submitted. Trigger, Triggered At, Tables and Served By are filled in only for responses received after an automatic mailing. Guest data columns are filled in if the response is linked to a guest profile. Response Filters responses Period The Period filter limits responses by the date they were received. The maximum date is the current day. Depending on the available data, responses can be filtered by the following parameters: Trigger date Response source Channel Who added — the employee who added the manual response, or the system; Served by — the employee associated with the event; Ratings — a rating value, including NPS, with a comparison condition (≥, >, ≤, <, =, ≠) or a range of values; if a response has several ratings, a match on at least one is sufficient; Tables Has text responses Device In the general table, the following are additionally available: Locations — including the option No location; Survey — filter by survey name. The list includes published and unpublished surveys; drafts are not displayed. Viewing a Response To open detailed information, click on the response row. responses The details window may display: Response number; Guest and their phone number; Location; Survey name; Date and time of response; Response source; Employee who added the manual response; Device; Check number, if the response is linked to a check; Tables; Employees who served the guest; Answers to the survey questions. Adding a Response Manually Manual addition is used when an employee conducts a survey on behalf of a guest, for example over the phone. responses Open the general Responses table. Click Add response. Select a Location. The list displays locations available to you. Select a Survey. Before selecting a location, this field is unavailable. The list displays only published surveys for the selected location. Enter the guest's primary phone number. Click Add response. If an active guest profile is found, the system will open the selected survey. Complete the survey on behalf of the guest and submit the answers. After submission, the system creates a new response and links it to the selected location, survey and guest. The source Entered manually is set for such a response. If an active guest profile is not found by the specified phone number, the system will show an error and will not allow starting the survey. Deleting a Response Responses can be deleted in two ways: select one or more responses with the checkboxes on the left and click Delete in the bar that appears above the table on the right; right-click the response row and select Delete. responses Confirm the deletion in the confirmation window. After deletion, the response receives the system status Deleted and is no longer used in working data. The system also reduces the number of responses for the survey and recalculates related guest metrics, auto-tags and segments. Deleting a response does not make the personal link available for retaking. When this link is opened again, the respondent will still see a message that the survey has already been completed.

text: Entering a Shift An hour before the scheduled start of the shift, the Start Shift button will appear and will be displayed until the scheduled end of the shift. Geolocation and Photos Before entering a shift you must: Connect to the establishment's Wi-Fi network; Enable geolocation; Grant the application access to geolocation. Otherwise, the application will think that you have not yet arrived at the establishment and will not allow you to start a shift. title: Survey Completion by Respondent
text: The respondent opens the survey via a link in a mobile device or computer browser. Starting Completion A survey can be opened via a public or personal link. A Public link is not tied to a specific guest. The survey can be completed via it multiple times. A Personal link is tied to a guest, has a limited validity period and allows the response to be submitted only once. If the survey is no longer published or the personal link has expired, a message about the survey's unavailability will be displayed. When reopening a personal link after successful submission, a message is displayed stating that the survey has already been completed. Navigating the Survey Navigation buttons are added automatically by the system and do not require configuration. Start — displayed on the start screen. Continue — moves to the next page. Back — returns to the previous page, if available in the current scenario. Submit — displayed on the last page and saves the response. If consent to the processing of personal data is enabled on the start screen, the Start button remains unavailable until the respondent checks the consent checkbox. After successful submission, the system displays the configured final screen. If a final screen is not added, a standard survey completion message is displayed. Response Validation When moving between pages and on submission, the system checks whether the required questions are filled in and whether the entered values match the required format. On submission, the system additionally verifies that the personal link is still valid and that a response has not previously been submitted through it. Saving Progress During completion, the entered data is saved on the device and in the respondent's browser for as long as the survey is available. If the respondent refreshes the page and the survey structure has not changed, completion will continue from the same place, and previously entered values will be preserved. Submitting a Response The respondent fills in the survey pages available to them. On the last page, they click Submit. The system verifies the data and the link. Upon successful verification, the answers to all questions are saved as a single response. The respondent proceeds to the final screen. Consent and Unsubscribe If the survey author added consent to the processing of personal data, the respondent must confirm it on the start screen before beginning the survey. If unsubscribing from surveys is available on the start or final screen, the respondent can: Click Unsubscribe. Confirm the action in a separate window. Return to the survey or complete the unsubscription. After confirmation, the guest stops receiving subsequent survey mailings. For anonymous completion via a public link, the unsubscribe block is not displayed. If the Survey Was Changed During Completion If the respondent has already opened the survey and its structure was changed: Before the page is refreshed, they continue working with the open version; After refreshing, the current version is loaded, and completion starts over. Structural changes include, for example, changing whether a question is required, removing a selected option, or changing text field restrictions. In the current version, an edge-case scenario is possible: if the respondent started completing the old version and submitted a response after the structure was changed, the interface may show successful completion, but the response will not be saved if the old data no longer matches the current structure.
description: How the survey is displayed to the respondent, how navigation, validation, progress saving and response submission work.

title: Surveys

title: Surveys
text: Surveys help you collect feedback from guests after a visit, obtain ratings and comments, and then analyze the responses in CosmosResto. A survey can be distributed via a public link or sent to specific guests through mailings. Received responses are saved in the Responses section and can be linked to the guest, the mailing, and the event after which the survey was sent. To get started, create a Survey, publish it, and select a distribution method. Main Usage Scenarios Surveys can be used for the following tasks: Collecting anonymous feedback via a public link, for example through a QR code, website or social networks; Sending personal surveys to guests via mailings; Collecting ratings of the visit, service or quality; Taking individual ratings into account in guest statistics; Analyzing responses by surveys, guests, sources, channels and related events. Survey List The list is divided into published and unpublished surveys. List Tabs Published — contains only surveys with the status Published. Unpublished — contains active surveys with the statuses Draft and Unpublished, as well as Deactivated. Survey Information in the List The table can display the following data: Creation date Publication date — date and time of the last publication. Displayed for published surveys and updated with each publication. Name Location Responses — the number of active responses for the survey. The value is not reset after unpublishing or republishing. In guest statistics — shows whether the survey has at least one question with the Include in guest statistics setting enabled. Author Last modified — date and time of the last save, as well as the employee who made the changes. Search and Filters Use the available filters to search for the survey you need. Search — searches by survey name. Enter at least 3 characters. Geo — leaves in the list surveys for the selected available locations. Author — filters surveys by the employee who created them. The list of authors depends on the active tab, the selected locations and your access rights. Last modified — limits the list by the date of the last modification. Has responses — allows you to show only surveys with responses or only surveys without responses. Status — available on the Unpublished tab and allows you to filter drafts, unpublished and deactivated surveys. Survey Statuses A survey can have one of four statuses. Draft — the survey has been created but has never been published. It can be configured, deleted or published. Respondents cannot complete such a survey. Published — the survey is available for completion and collecting responses. The public link is active, and the survey can be used in mailings. Unpublished — collection of new responses is stopped. Previously received responses are retained. The survey can be modified and republished. Deactivated — the survey has been permanently withdrawn from use. It is retained for viewing history and responses, but editing and republishing are unavailable. Survey Lifecycle Create the survey. The system will save it with the status Draft. Publish the survey. The status will change to Published, and response collection will begin. If necessary, unpublish the survey. The status will change to Unpublished, and new responses will stop coming in. If necessary, republish the unpublished survey. If the survey should no longer be used, deactivate it. A deactivated survey cannot be returned to use. A survey in any status can be duplicated. The copy is always created as a new draft. Publication settings and previously received responses are not carried over to the copy.
description: A tool for creating surveys, collecting feedback from guests and analyzing the received responses.

title: Templates
text: Templates are used for WhatsApp mailings. Messages are sent with the text of the selected template - entering custom text is not possible. After a template is created, CosmosResto automatically sends it for approval to Meta via Twilio. Once Meta approves the template, it can be selected for a mailing. Template List templates To open the list, go to Marketing → Mailings and click Templates. Template statuses: On Approval - the template has been sent for approval, no decision yet Approved - the template has been approved and can be selected in a mailing Rejected - the template did not pass approval. It cannot be used in a mailing The Search field searches by template name. To create a template, click Create. For details, see Create Template. Template Page templates The template page shows the template name, language, text, buttons, and a message preview. A template cannot be changed after it is created. To adjust the text or buttons, create a copy: click the duplicate button next to Delete. The creation form opens, filled in with the data of the original template. Enter a new name, make the changes, and send the copy for approval. The copy goes through approval again, even if the original template has already been approved. The original template and the mailings that use it do not change. A template can be deleted in any status. The exception is a template selected in a mailing or a mailing draft: such a template cannot be deleted. Table Settings To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ Select the columns to display ✔ Change the column order - drag a column in the list by the icon to the left of its name ✔ Pin the required columns - click the pin icon to the right of the column name. Pinned columns move to the beginning of the table ✔ Restore the default settings using Reset to Default templates The template table contains the following columns: Name Language - the template language, RU or EN Template Text Status Author Created At Last Update Data Filtering templates Click Filters to select templates by Status and Language. You can select several values in each filter. After selecting the required values, click Apply.

title: Waitlist
text: Waitlist helps you save a guest request when the establishment cannot yet confirm a standard reservation. For example, a suitable table is occupied, the required time is not available or placement conditions are still being clarified. A record on the waitlist does not reserve a table or block time. When a suitable spot becomes available, the record can be converted to a standard reservation. Waitlist is available in the Timeline, Floor Plan and Reservations Table views. On the Timeline and Floor Plan, a separate list is displayed with a counter of active records. Waitlist does not guarantee the guest a visit to the establishment. Until the record is converted to a standard reservation, the table and time interval remain free for other reservations. When to Use Waitlist Guest submitted a request, but you cannot yet confirm a reservation; Guest contacted directly, but no suitable table or time is available now; An existing reservation can no longer be saved in its current form, but the guest is ready to consider another time or placement conditions. How a Record Gets on Waitlist Converting from a request to a reservation with status Waitlist. Creating manually in the reservation module by specifying status Waitlist. Changing the status of an existing reservation to Waitlist. Creating a Record from a Request Open the request. Select request confirmation. Set status Waitlist. Save the changes. After saving, the request becomes inactive and a record appears on the waitlist. Creating a Record Manually Open any view of the reservation module. Click Add Reservation. Fill in guest data. Specify date, time and number of guests. Select a table if necessary, this is not a required field. Select status Waitlist. Click Save. Converting a Reservation to Waitlist The process is similar to changing a reservation status. After saving, the table is freed and the record is moved to the waitlist. Open the reservation. Change status to Waitlist. Save the changes. Converting a Record from Waitlist to Reservation Open a record with status Waitlist. Select a table, if it was not previously specified. Change status to Not confirmed, Confirmed or In progress. Save the changes. After this a standard reservation is created. Canceling a Record Open the record. Change status to Cancelled. Specify the reason. Confirm the action. The reason for cancellation is required. Waitlist cancellation reasons match reservation cancellation reasons. A cancelled record cannot be recovered.
